papers.abstract: Combination immunotherapy targeting the coinhibitory molecules TIGIT and PD-L1 promotes non-exhausted CD8+ T cell differentiation in cancer. Because anti-TIGIT efficacy requires Fc binding, we investigated the role of Fcγ receptor (FcγR)-expressing myeloid cells in the mechanism of action. Conventional dendritic cells (cDCs) were required for therapeutic efficacy. Transcriptional profiling of intratumoral myeloid cells revealed an FcγR+ cDC type-1 (cDC1)-like activation state characterized by elevated costimulatory ligands for CD28 (CD80/CD86) and CD226 (PVR) that was enriched in Fc-active anti-TIGIT combination-treated tumors. Therapy-expanded CD8+ T cells expressed CD28 and upregulated CD226 upon treatment. Mechanistically, CD28 signaling was a prerequisite for therapy-induced CD226 expression on T cells, and cDC-derived PVR promoted CD226-mediated non-exhausted T cell differentiation. Type I interferon (IFN-I), induced through FcγR engagement, maintained and amplified the FcγR+ cDC1-like state, and exogenous IFN-I rescued anti-tumor immunity upon Fc-inert anti-TIGIT and anti-PD-L1 combination. Thus, Fc-active anti-TIGIT and anti-PD-L1 therapy promotes a sequential costimulatory cascade centered on cDCs, amplified by IFN-I signaling.

papers.abstract: Research is an integral component of Canadian radiation oncology (RO) residency training. Reports suggest increasing RO resident publication rates, but national trends remain underexplored. This study examined residency research productivity and predictors over a 25-year period. A database was compiled including graduating residents from Canadian RO residency programs between 1998 and 2023. Demographic information was extracted from public sources. PubMed-indexed publications during medical school and residency were identified and categorized by journal, research type, authorship position and impact factor (IF). Graduates were divided into six temporal cohorts. Linear and chi-square trend tests analyzed rates over time. Univariable and multivariable regression analyses identified authorship predictors. Among 416 graduates (43% female), 970 residency publications were identified (52% first-author). Retrospective studies were most common (29%). The proportion of publishing residents increased from 29.1% (1998-2002) to 80.8% (2020-2023) (p 4 increased significantly over time. Later graduation cohorts, larger programs, and two specific residency programs predicted higher resident research output (p < 0.05), whereas gender did not. Medical school research productivity correlated positively with residency output. Canadian RO resident research productivity has increased markedly over 25-years, with predictors including more recent graduation cohorts, larger program size and training program. These findings establish a contemporary benchmark for Canadian RO research productivity.

papers.abstract: The study evaluated the risk of grade ≥2 acute diarrhea of modern bowel-sparing intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT)-based neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) versus three-dimensional conformal radiotherapy (3DCRT)-based nCRT. In this open-label, historically controlled, multicenter, single-arm phase II trial, patients with LARC, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-2, and adequate organ function were recruited. Protocol treatment involved concurrent capecitabine and IMRT, consisting of 45 Gy (25 fractions) for elective nodes and an optional 5.4 Gy (3 fractions) boost for gross disease. Bowel-sparing constraints included small-bowel volume receiving 15 Gy (V15Gy) of <200 cc. Acute toxicities were graded in the protocol-defined primary outcome window. Grade ≥2 acute diarrhea was tested against a 26% historical benchmark from phase II trials of 3DCRT-based nCRT with capecitabine with a one-sided α-level of 0.05 and 80% power. Fifty-five patients were enrolled, including 48 patients with stage III disease and 25 patients with a positive circumferential resection margin on magnetic resonance imaging. Fifty-four patients (98.2%) completed protocol-defined nCRT. The median small-bowel V15Gy was 85 cc (interquartile range, 47-105). Grade ≥2 acute diarrhea occurred in four patients (7.3%; 90% confidence interval, 2.5-15.9; p 1 mm rates were 6.0% and 88.0%, respectively, with grade ≥2 postoperative complications observed in 14% of patients. After median follow-up of 14 months, the 12-month locoregional progression-free and overall survival rates were 95.0% and 98.2%, respectively. Modern bowel-sparing IMRT in nCRT for LARC was associated with a low rate of grade ≥2 acute diarrhea with no obvious unfavorable signals for resectability, locoregional control, or safety; however, longer follow-up is needed to assess mature oncologic outcomes and late toxicities.

papers.abstract: The CNS tumor classification of the WHO currently subsumes subependymomas (SE) of the supratentorial, infratentorial, and spinal compartment as one tumor type. Molecular data on SE are generally sparse, but SE are known to exhibit distinct global DNA methylation profiles according to their anatomical location. Previous studies indicate that a fraction of posterior fossa tumors exhibiting DNA methylation profiles of SE morphologically appear as ependymomas and may be prone to relapse. We assembled a cohort of ependymal tumors that best match supratentorial (n = 89), infratentorial (n = 146), or spinal (n = 45) SE DNA methylation profiles. Infratentorial tumors with an SE DNA methylation profile occurred at significantly higher ages with a male to female ratio of 4:1 and displayed two distinct subtypes. One of them (n = 49) was enriched for tumors that morphologically appear as ependymomas, carrying a loss of chromosome 6 as well as TERT promoter mutations. Respective patients showed a significantly shorter progression-free survival (p = 0.00014). Supratentorial SE frequently showed chromosome 8 loss while a small subset of tumors with a distinct DNA methylation profile and a segmentation of chromosome 6 was detected. Such chromosomal abnormalities were similarly observed in spinal SE. Based on clustering analysis and clinical features of tumors best matching a subependymoma methylation class, we postulate four subtypes of subependymomas. A fifth, previously undefined type of infratentorial ependymomas was provisionally named PFC. It showed frequent relapses but was distinct from PFA and PFB ependymomas.

papers.abstract: Uterine carcinosarcoma is a rare, aggressive malignancy with high rates of distant failure, and the optimal sequencing of adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation in locally advanced disease is undefined. We evaluated whether the sequencing of adjuvant therapies is associated with overall survival (OS) in surgically managed FIGO stage III-IVA uterine carcinosarcoma. We identified 4593 patients with surgically treated FIGO stage III-IVA uterine carcinosarcoma in the National Cancer Database (2004-2020). Patients were categorized as chemotherapy only (CO), radiation only (RO), sequential chemoradiation (SCRT), concurrent chemoradiation (CRT), or no adjuvant therapy. CRT was defined as chemotherapy and radiation start dates within 14 days, with SCRT separated by more than 14 days. OS was estimated by Kaplan-Meier and compared using Cox regression, with inverse probability of treatment weighting, propensity-score matching, and landmark analyses as sensitivity analyses. SCRT had the highest 2-year OS (67.3%) versus CO (51.4%), CRT (52.8%), and RO (34.6%). On MVA, SCRT was associated with improved OS versus CO (adjusted HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.60-0.82; univariable HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.61-0.74), whereas CRT was not (HR 1.12, 95% CI 0.80-1.57). SCRT benefit persisted across weighted, matched, and landmark analyses and after exclusion of stage IVA patients (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.59-0.80). Age and lymphovascular space invasion were independently prognostic. In locally advanced uterine carcinosarcoma, SCRT was associated with superior OS compared with CO, while CRT was not. These data support prospective evaluation of adjuvant treatment sequencing in this histology.

papers.abstract: To evaluate national trends in time to treatment initiation (TTI) for cervical cancer from 2004 to 2022, and to identify factors associated with treatment delay. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the National Cancer Database. Adult women with cervical cancer diagnosed between 2004 and 2022 were included and categorized by initial treatment as radiation-based, surgery, or chemotherapy. TTI was defined as the interval from diagnosis to first treatment. Multivariable quantile regression models evaluated temporal trends and factors associated with longer TTI. Covariates included patient sociodemographic and treating facility characteristics. Among patients receiving radiation-based treatment, secondary analyses evaluated the association between TTI and completion of radiation within 56 days. A total of 73,233 patients were included: 43,995 in the radiation-based group, 26,735 in the surgery group, and 2503 in the chemotherapy-only group. Median TTI increased over time across all three modalities, from 29 to 45 days in the radiation-based group, 39 to 57 days in the surgery group, and 23.5 to 39 days in the chemotherapy-only group, corresponding to relative increases of 55.2%, 46.2%, and 66.0%, respectively. Longer TTI was consistently associated with treatment at high uninsured/Medicaid burden facilities, Medicaid insurance, Hispanic ethnicity, lower neighborhood educational attainment, and diagnosis-treatment facility discordance. Longer TTI was not associated with prolonged radiation duration beyond 56 days. TTI for cervical cancer has lengthened nationally across treatment pathways. Delays reflect structural inequities and care fragmentation. Further work is needed to benchmark TTI cutoff and quantify harm.

papers.abstract: Early-onset pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (EO-PanNETs) exhibit distinct clinical features, but their metabolic profiles and age-related associations remain poorly understood. This study included 641 patients with PanNETs from four tertiary centers in China. EO-PanNETs were defined as PanNETs diagnosed before 50 years. 1,282 hospital-based nonmalignant controls were matched 1:2 by age and sex. Conditional logistic regression and Cox models were used to assess associations with PanNET occurrence and survival outcomes, respectively. Age-related effect modification was assessed using exposure-by-age interaction terms, with age modeled continuously using restricted cubic splines (RCS) in sensitivity analyses. Compared with late-onset cases, EO-PanNETs exhibited a higher prevalence of reduced high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (29.2% vs 17.8%, P < 0.001). Although the overall prevalence of diabetes was similar between EO-PanNETs and LO-PanNETs, the proportion of new-onset cases among patients with diabetes was higher in EO-PanNETs(71.4% vs. 44.8%, P = 0.018). In case-control analyses using matched nonmalignant controls as reference, alcohol intake (OR, 1.77 vs. 0.79; P interaction = 0.008), diabetes mellitus (OR, 9.72 vs. 3.34; P interaction = 0.048) and elevated triglycerides (OR, 1.75 vs. 1.01; P interaction = 0.023) showed stronger associations with PanNET occurrence in younger individuals. EO-PanNETs also exhibited better overall survival and progression-free survival than LO-PanNETs. RCS analyses further identified age-related differences in the associations of alcohol intake and overweight with PanNET occurrence. These findings highlight age-related differences in the associations of metabolic factors with PanNETs, providing new insights into age-related metabolic heterogeneity in this rare disease.

papers.abstract: This study reports on analytical and clinical validation of the highly automated Ion Torrent™ Oncomine™ Dx Express Test (ODxET) for detecting PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered tumors in patients with hormone receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer that may benefit from treatment with capivasertib plus fulvestrant. Analytical validation studies were completed using commercially sourced breast cancer tissue specimens to establish the ODxET assay detection capability (limit of detection, limit of blank), precision (repeatability, reproducibility), and effect of endogenous interfering substances for detecting PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations. Clinical validation was performed using 429 residual breast cancer tissue samples from the Phase 3 CAPItello-291 trial and progression-free survival (PFS) was analyzed for patients with PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered tumors, as detected by ODxET, and compared to efficacy outcomes from the CAPItello-291 study. Comparison of assay agreement between ODxET and FoundationOne®CDx (F1CDx) gave an overall, positive and negative percent agreement of 89.2%, 82.0%, and 96.6%, respectively. The 18% false negative rate observed with ODxET was largely attributable to limited detection of complex PTEN variants. PFS benefit was observed with capivasertib plus fulvestrant versus placebo plus fulvestrant in patients with PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered tumors detected by ODxET (n=162; hazard ratio 0.55, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.38-0.78). This is similar to the observed PFS benefit in the population with PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered tumors identified by F1CDx in the CAPItello-291 trial (hazard ratio 0.49, 95% CI: 0.38-0.64). This study demonstrates the clinical utility of ODxET to identify patients with PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered tumors that may benefit from treatment with capivasertib plus fulvestrant.

papers.abstract: Surgical management of cervical cancer has changed substantially over the past decade as randomized and prospective data have refined the extent of resection, the role of fertility-sparing surgery, nodal assessment strategies, and the choice of surgical approach. This Society of Gynecologic Oncology evidence-based review addresses the upfront surgical management of cervical cancer. Surgery for recurrent disease, including pelvic exenteration and resection of oligometastatic recurrence, is outside its scope. A panel of gynecologic oncologists and subject matter experts identified twelve clinical questions spanning extent of resection, fertility-sparing surgery, lymph node assessment, surgical approach, and the integration of surgery with chemoradiation. Relevant literature was systematically collected and synthesized, and each recommendation was assigned a strength of recommendation and quality of evidence using a two-part rating system adapted from the ASCCP guidelines. Recommendations were approved by the SGO Clinical Practice Committee, Document Review Panel, and Board of Directors. Simple hysterectomy with nodal assessment is preferred for low-risk FIGO 2018 stage IA through IB1 disease. Fertility-sparing surgery is acceptable for appropriately selected patients with low-risk stage IA1 through IB1 tumors, with conization or simple trachelectomy preferred over radical trachelectomy. Sentinel lymph node biopsy may replace complete pelvic lymphadenectomy when an accepted algorithm is applied, with indocyanine green and near-infrared imaging the preferred mapping technique. When radical hysterectomy is indicated, the open approach is preferred outside of a clinical trial. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by surgery is not recommended in place of chemoradiation, and hysterectomy after completion of definitive chemoradiation is not recommended in the absence of documented residual disease. Evidence quality varies considerably across questions, and several recommendations rest on observational data or expert consensus.

papers.abstract: To develop and validate an artificial intelligence-enabled platform that combines efficient screening with explicit eligibility logic by converting unstructured cancer trial criteria into reusable structured queries, and illustrates potential eligibility using synthetic patients. We downloaded actively recruiting US interventional treatment trials for advanced/metastatic breast cancer, colon cancer, and non-small cell lung cancer from ClinicalTrials.gov. Medical oncologists created 24 synthetic patient vignettes. A large language model converted trial eligibility criteria into Structured Query Language (SQL) code and patient information into structured records, enabling rule-based matching without further LLM inference. Cancer details and treatment history were considered, but not laboratory results or comorbidities. Validation included physician editing of generated eligibility code for 30 trials and independent assessments by two physicians, followed by consensus adjudication, for eligibility across ten trials. We descriptively summarized potential eligibility by trial characteristics and when varying age, ECOG performance status, sex, and ZIP code. Of 833 candidate trials, 746 met inclusion criteria. Performing matching for all 746 trials took a median of 0.459 seconds per patient, excluding patient-data preparation. Against physician consensus, automated matching agreed on 230/240 patient-trial pairs (95.8%; sensitivity 83.3%, specificity 100%). Across synthetic patients, potentially eligible trials ranged from 10 to 258 without geographic restrictions. Counts decreased with worse performance status and geographic restriction and were relatively stable across ages 30-90. Later-phase, randomized, and molecularly selective trials generally matched fewer vignettes. LLM-generated SQL enables rapid, explicit rule-based screening for potential trial eligibility. Evaluation in synthetic vignettes supports feasibility, while missed matches underscore the need for further validation.

papers.abstract: Ovarian clear cell carcinoma is a rare but aggressive and biologically distinct subtype of ovarian cancer, in which PIK3CA mutations are common. Advanced ovarian clear cell carcinoma is very difficult to treat, and after failure of platinum-based chemotherapy, therapeutic options are limited. We aimed to evaluate the anti-tumour activity and safety of the PI3Kα inhibitor, risovalisib, for treatment of patients with recurrent or persistent PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma. We conducted a single-arm, phase 2 trial of the PI3Kα inhibitor, risovalisib, in 27 centres in China and 12 centres in Japan. Eligible participants were adult patients (aged 18 years or older, with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1) with recurrent or persistent PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma and one to three lines of previous systemic anti-tumour treatment. Risovalisib was given orally at 40 mg daily in 21-day cycles until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or other protocol-defined reasons for discontinuation. The primary endpoint was objective response rate assessed by blinded independent review committee (BIRC) using Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (version 1.1), among all treated patients with a confirmed PIK3CA hotspot mutation and baseline tumour assessments with measurable lesions per BIRC (efficacy analysis set). The primary endpoint was considered met if the lower 95% CI was greater than 8%. Safety analyses were performed in all patients who received at least one dose of risovalisib (safety analysis set). The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05043922) and is ongoing but no longer recruiting patients. Between Oct 6, 2021, and Jan 31, 2024, 93 patients were enrolled and received risovalisib. The median age was 49 years (IQR 43-58), all patients were female, 52 (56%) were from Japan, 41 (44%) were from China, and 63 (68%) had two or more previous lines of therapy. The median duration of follow-up was 14·5 months (IQR 8·6-18·3). The objective response rate was 29 (35% [95% CI 25-46]) of 84 patients in the efficacy analysis set. The most commonly reported grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events in 93 patients were rash (30 [32%]), hyperglycaemia (28 [30%]), and decreased weight (7 [8%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 36 (39%) patients, the most common being rash (eight [9%]), pneumonitis (six [6%]), and decreased appetite (four [4%]). There were no treatment-related deaths. These results support risovalisib as a potential novel treatment option for PIK3CA-mutated ovarian clear cell carcinoma, a rare yet lethal cancer in dire need of additional treatment options. Combination strategies including risovalisib could also be explored to further increase efficacy observed in this study. Haihe Biopharma.

papers.abstract: Sjögren's syndrome creates a lymphoma-prone inflammatory niche and confers one of the highest autoimmune risks of B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Yet the genetic and cellular mechanisms that remodel this pre-neoplastic niche into a tumor-supportive immune microenvironment remain unclear. We integrated human genetics, single-cell transcriptomics and functional cell biology to identify an actionable mediator of this transition. We combined bidirectional Mendelian randomization, directionality filtering, MHC-exclusion sensitivity analyses (chromosome 6: 25-35 Mb), colocalization and summary-based HLA fine-mapping. Single-cell RNA sequencing of salivary gland and splenic marginal-zone lymphoma was used to localize genetic risk, reconstruct cross-disease B-cell states and infer intercellular signaling. Mechanistic dependence was tested in IFN-γ-stimulated Raji B-lymphoma cells, and clinical relevance was evaluated in a public chronic lymphocytic leukemia cohort. Genetic liability to Sjögren's syndrome increased marginal-zone/MALT, diffuse large B-cell and overall non-Hodgkin lymphoma risk, and effects collapsed after MHC exclusion and resolved to the class II 8.1 ancestral haplotype. Single-cell analysis localized risk to salivary B cells and revealed disease-associated remodeling toward a lymphoid, MIF-rich, CD74-receiving microenvironment, with plasma cells as the largest MIF source. HLA-class-II/CD74 programs increased along the Sjögren-to-lymphoma B-cell trajectory. In Raji cells, MIF activated AKT/NF-κB/BCL-xL signaling and viability. ISO-1 or CD74 knockdown suppressed the pathway and increased cleaved PARP, whereas AKT activation partially rescued signaling and viability. Higher CD74 expression marked adverse outcome in an external B-cell malignancy cohort. Convergent genetic, single-cell and perturbation evidence positions CD74 as a candidate organizer of a lymphoma-supportive immune microenvironment linking inherited MHC class II risk to B-cell survival. The MIF-CD74 axis provides a translational tumor-microenvironment target that requires tissue-level and prospective validation.

papers.abstract: Post-ICU care often misses patients unable to attend in-person clinic visits. Remote assessments of physical function might increase access to ICU aftercare. We investigated whether patient-reported disability predicts handgrip strength (HGS) and the 2-Minute Walk Test (2MWT) distance with sufficient clinical accuracy. This secondary analysis of the stepped-wedge cluster-randomised Enhanced Recovery after Intensive Care trial included patients from 10 German ICU clusters who completed the WHO Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS) 2.0 plus either HGS, the 2MWT, or both, 6 months after ICU discharge. Relationships between WHODAS 2.0, HGS, and 2MWT were analysed using scatter plots, correlation coefficients, linear regressions, and Bland-Altman plots. Predictions of HGS and the 2MWT were compared with the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for both measures. Of 1463 enrolled patients, 620 were analysed. The median WHODAS 2.0 sum score was 11 (Q1, Q3: 3, 22). The median HGS, expressed as a percentage of the expected value (%exp), was 70.6%exp (Q1, Q3: 54.4, 85.6), and the median 2MWT distance was 73.7%exp (Q1, Q3: 61.5, 85.8). The 2MWT was not completed by 59% of patients. Higher disability was moderately correlated with lower HGS (Spearman %exp: -0.41) and shorter 2MWT distance (Spearman %exp: -0.47). In multivariable regression models, the WHODAS 2.0 sum score predicted HGS in kg (β: -0.27 [95% CI: -0.33 to -0.22]; P<0.001) and 2MWT distance in m (β: -1.94 [95% CI: -2.37 to -1.51]; P<0.001), but the limits of agreement exceeded the MCIDs. With increasing disability, HGS and 2MWT performance declined, although correlations were moderate and uncertainty of predictions exceeded MCIDs of both instruments. Remote WHODAS 2.0 assessments cannot replace in-person physical function testing. NCT03671447.

papers.abstract: In IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, prognostic biomarkers beyond MGMT promoter methylation remain limited. Chromosome 14q contains candidate tumor suppressors, yet the significance of arm-level 14q loss in molecularly defined glioblastoma is unclear. Arm-level 14q status was inferred from coordinated 14q expression (Gaussian-mixture model) in bulk RNA sequencing of 215 Japanese IDH-wildtype glioblastomas and validated against methylation-array copy number (n = 42). Associations with outcome and transcriptional programs were evaluated and assessed in CGGA (n = 74) and TCGA (n = 139) using the discovery-cohort threshold. RNA-seq-based calls agreed with array copy number in 40/42 cases (κ = 0.90). 14q loss (87/215, 40.5%) was associated with shorter overall (p = 0.0053) and progression-free survival (p = 0.0175), remaining prognostic in the prespecified multivariable model (hazard ratio 1.44, 95% confidence interval 1.02-2.01; p = 0.036). 14q loss and MGMT promoter hypomethylation were prognostically complementary (four-group p < 0.0001). Chromosome 14-excluded, purity-adjusted gene set enrichment analysis showed increased E2F-target and G2M-checkpoint and reduced oxidative-phosphorylation and lipid-metabolism programs in 14q-loss tumors. The survival association was reproduced in CGGA (p = 0.0012) but not in TCGA (p = 0.55), with significant heterogeneity (interaction p = 0.005). RNA-seq-inferable 14q loss identifies a clinically adverse subgroup of Japanese IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, is complementary to MGMT promoter methylation, and is associated with a proliferation-high, oxidative-phosphorylation-low transcriptional state. The absence of this association in TCGA underscores the need for validation in additional population-diverse cohorts before clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: Measurable residual disease (MRD) assessment is central to risk stratification, response evaluation, and relapse detection in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). However, substantial global variability in its methodology and implementation persists. Differences in sampling strategies, detection methods, reporting thresholds, and interpretation criteria hinder cross-trial comparability and clinical standardization. To address this, an international expert panel representing major pediatric and adult study groups and reference laboratories developed consensus recommendations, using a structured current-practices survey followed by a multi-round Delphi process. Consensus was achieved on 38 of 41 statements. Recommendations span three domains: pre-analytical requirements, technical and nomenclature standards, and MRD-based remission and relapse definitions. Bone marrow was endorsed as the reference specimen for MRD assessment, and MRD was prioritized over cytomorphology in cases of discordance. Principles for risk- and actionability-guided late MRD monitoring, confirmation of MRD reappearance, and MRD-informed relapse assessment were also defined. Among the key technical consensus statements, a standardized MRD assay nomenclature was adopted. Areas without consensus-namely, anticoagulant choice for PCR-based MRD, interpretation of isolated BCR::ABL1 reconversion, and the exclusive use of MRD to define remission-highlight ongoing biological and clinical complexity. This guideline, applicable across all ages, provides a practical framework to standardize MRD assessment in ALL and support MRD-guided clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract: Kirsten rat sarcoma (KRAS), the most frequently altered oncogene, is a key target for T cell-based therapies. Mutant KRAS (mKRAS)-specific T cell receptors (TCRs) enable targeted treatment for patients with matching mKRAS/HLA allele pairs. We generated a TCR warehouse library covering approximately one-quarter of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients and 10% of colorectal cancer patients. Warehouse TCRs exhibit strong avidities and cytotoxicity, comparable to existing benchmark TCRs. Detailed characterization of each TCR revealed unique biology for specific KRAS neoantigens. TCRs with high sensitivity for KRAS G12V/HLA-C*01:02 also recognize the wild-type epitope. However, the wild-type epitope abundance appears to be significantly lower, potentially creating a therapeutic window, albeit necessitating deeper evaluation. Additionally, we show that TCRs recognize KRAS G12V on HLA-C*03:03 and HLA-C*03:04 interchangeably, thereby resulting in a single neoantigen with one of the highest frequencies. In summary, this mKRAS-targeted TCR library comprises candidates for further preclinical and clinical development.

papers.abstract: To develop an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) model to predict the complete/partial response of oligometastatic brain lesions from melanoma (MBMs) two months after from radiosurgical or fractionated stereotactic treatments. 50 consecutive patients with a total 102 MBMs treated with CyberKnife® SBRT from December 2012 to December 2018 were selected within the Rabbit study. Local response was evaluated on brain MRI performed during follow-up using response evaluation criteria in solid tumors (RECIST) and revised using response criteria for brain metastases from the response assessment in neuro-oncology criteria (RANO) group. For each treated lesion, the following variables were considered: number of treated lesions, the LDH pre-treatment level, previous treatments (surgery or whole brain RT), BRAF status, time from primary diagnosis to brain lesions discovery (Time_diag), lesion dimensions and site, SBRT dose and fractionation, type of concomitant treatment with ipilimumab (IPI). Six different supervised machine learning models, including logistic regression (LR), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), decision tree (DT) and light gradient boosting (LGBM), were trained and internally validated with 5-fold cross validation. Model performances were assessed using receiving operator curves (ROC) and area under the curve (AUC). An explainable approach based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was deployed to generate individual explanations of the model decisions. Lastly, a decision tree was created to better understand and interpret the complex relationships between the covariates and the target variable. 23.5% of lesions had a complete or partial response and were used as ground truth for the ML models. The best performing model was the LGBM, reporting a mean AUCs in the 5-fold cross validation of 0.87 (0.85-0.91). SHAP analysis strongly associated complete/partial response with four variables, namely in order of importance: the BRAF status, the total dose, the type of treatment with ipilimumab, and the lesion dimension. In particular, the DT classified patients with BRAF "wild-type" status having only 10.7% probability to reach complete/partial response. Among these lesions, those treated with doses < 24 Gy had 0% probability of complete/partial response. By contrast, lesions with a BRAF "mutated" status reported a probability of complete/partial response of 39.1%. Among these lesions, those treated with concomitant ipilimumab reached 100% probability of complete/partial response. Machine-learning models enable a reliable prediction of the treatment response of oligometastatic lesions receiving SBRT. This approach may assist radiation oncologists to tailor more individualized treatment plans in this clinical setting. An external validation of the results is mandatory.

papers.abstract: Monoclonal antibody (mAb)-based therapies have revolutionized cancer treatment; however, their clinical efficacy is often limited by insufficient antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC), tumor antigen escape, and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). To overcome these limitations, we developed an allogeneic stem cell-derived invariant natural killer T (NKT) cell platform engineered to express a high-affinity non-cleavable CD16 receptor (CD16HSC-NKT) for broad enhancement of mAb-based immunotherapy. Using a clinically guided differentiation platform, we generated highly pure and scalable CD16HSC-NKT cells exhibiting robust expression of NK receptors, potent cytotoxic machinery, and a Th1-biased cytokine profile. CD16HSC-NKT cells demonstrated potent intrinsic antitumor activity and potently enhanced the efficacy of multiple therapeutic antibodies, including Trastuzumab, Tafasitamab, Rituximab, Daratumumab, and Cusatuzumab, across diverse hematologic and solid tumor models. In vivo, combination therapy induced durable tumor eradication and prolonged survival in xenograft models, outperforming the clinically approved antibody-drug conjugate trastuzumab deruxtecan. Mechanistically, therapeutic antibodies promoted the expansion, persistence, and activation of CD16HSC-NKT cells within tumors. CD16HSC-NKT uniquely remodeled the TME by selectively depleting CD1d-expressing tumor-associated macrophages and myeloid-derived suppressor cells. CD16HSC-NKT cells also exhibited minimal alloreactivity, no graft-versus-host disease, and no detectable systemic toxicity. Collectively, these findings establish CD16HSC-NKT cells as a safe, off-the-shelf cellular platform capable of broadly enhancing monoclonal antibody therapy through sustained ADCC, multimodal tumor targeting, and TME remodeling.

papers.abstract: Interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis is a safety concern with trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd). We characterized post-onset changes in ILD severity and imaging patterns, and explored potential prognostic factors for fatal T-DXd-related ILD in Japanese patients with breast or gastric cancer. This post hoc analysis included 381 independently adjudicated T-DXd-related ILD cases from two Japanese all-patient post-marketing surveillance studies. We described transitions from onset to worst Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events grade and imaging pattern changes. Exploratory tumor type-stratified Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess factors associated with time to fatal (Grade 5) ILD. The variable with the highest hazard ratio (HR) and each of the remaining significant univariate factors (p < 0.05 or a 95% confidence interval excluding 1) meeting the criteria were included in two-covariate multivariable models. At ILD onset, 60.1% of patients had Grade 1 ILD. Overall, 30 of the 381 adjudicated ILD cases (7.9%) progressed to fatal Grade 5, initially presenting with Grade 1 (n = 9), 2 (n = 5), or 3 (n = 16); time to death was 3-173 days. Of 24 cases with imaging pattern changes, 14 transitioned from nondiffuse alveolar damage (non-DAD) to DAD (10 were fatal). Abnormal C-reactive protein (CRP) at onset had the highest HR in univariate analyses. In separate CRP-adjusted two-covariate multivariable models, preexisting ILD and several onset factors (dyspnea; abnormal SpO2/lactate dehydrogenase/Krebs von den Lungen-6; pleural/cardiac effusion; DAD pattern; traction bronchiectasis) were associated with fatal ILD. An organizing pneumonia pattern was associated with a lower hazard. T-DXd-related ILD may progress rapidly to fatal outcomes, even from low-grade or non-DAD presentations, and several onset factors (e.g., elevated CRP, decreased SpO2, and DAD pattern) were associated with fatal ILD outcomes. These findings are exploratory and should not be used to determine whether to initiate or withhold corticosteroids. Guideline-concordant ILD management remains essential regardless of these factors, while their potential role in identifying patients requiring closer monitoring warrants further validation. The breast cancer and the gastric cancer surveys were registered at the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp/en-top) under the identifiers jRCT1080225197 and jRCT2001200001, respectively.

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma is orchestrated by pacemaker cancer cells, a rare population preferentially residing at the hubs of tumor cell networks. These cells autonomously generate periodic Ca2+ oscillations that drive glioblastoma network function, resilience, and disease progression. To date, the Ca2+-activated K+ channel KCa3.1 is the only known driver of pacemaker function, calling for studies to identify additional factors - to better understand a key component of glioblastoma pathobiology, and uncover novel therapeutic targets. A molecular Ca2+ integrator technology enabled the transcriptional profiling of highly Ca2+-active glioblastoma cells, a population enriched for pacemaker cells. Putative regulators of pacemaker function were interrogated using genetic, pharmacological, and computational approaches across complementary glioblastoma models. We identified a distinct transcriptional program that captures highly Ca2+ active glioblastoma cells, including pacemaker cells, across preclinical models and human glioblastoma specimens. This program comprised upregulated cholesterol biosynthesis enzymes, TM-network markers (Aquaporin-4 and Cystatin C), and the Ca2+-activated K+ channels KCa1.1 and KCa2.3. Amongst these components, in silico modeling identified KCa2.3 as the only channel compatible with executing pacemaker function. Consistently, KCa2.3 expression was increased in pacemaker cells, and both genetic and pharmacological perturbation of KCa2.3 selectively disrupted pacemaker function, resulting in reduced network-wide Ca2+ activity. Ultimately, pharmacological inhibition of KCa2.3 with edelfosine reduced tumor burden in human brain spheroids. We present the first experimental approach to characterize molecular factors of glioblastoma pacemaker cells in a broad and unbiased manner, and identify KCa2.3 as a novel pacemaker gene and promising therapeutic target.

papers.abstract: Chidamide is an oral histone deacetylase inhibitor whose use as early maintenance after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) remains insufficiently defined. This prospective single-center Phase 1/2 cohort included all 47 patients enrolled and treated by March 31, 2026. The Phase 2 primary endpoint was 2-year leukemia-free survival (LFS). An exploratory observational comparison used 23 platform-compatible historical comparators, time-dependent maintenance exposure, and propensity-score overlap weighting. Both cohorts received chidamide-containing conditioning. No formal multiplicity adjustment was applied. Treated-cohort 2-year LFS was 78.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 63.9%-87.9%). In the main weighted model, maintenance exposure was associated with lower hazards of death (hazard ratio [HR], 0.29; 95% CI, 0.09-0.96) and relapse or death (HR, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.09-0.63). LFS associations were more consistent across sensitivity analyses; overall survival was less stable in landmark analyses. Graft-versus-host disease-free/relapse-free survival remained inconclusive. Maintenance began a median of 16 days after HSCT; 45 of 47 patients reached 20 mg twice weekly, and 35 completed 365 days. Grade 3-4 treatment-emergent adverse events were documented in 37 patients, predominantly cytopenias. One patient died during maintenance from infection with transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy; the relationship to chidamide was not determined. Relapse, non-relapse mortality, and lymphocyte subset recovery were descriptive. Maintenance was deliverable with active dose management. papers.abstract: Breastfeeding has been found to be associated with decreased ovarian cancer risk, but prospective analyses are sparse and limited by insufficient sample sizes to assess associations by histotype and patient characteristics. To investigate the association between breastfeeding (ever/never, duration, and timing) and incident epithelial ovarian cancer risk overall and by histotype, we leveraged harmonized individual-level data from 11 prospective cohort studies participating in the Ovarian Cancer Cohort Consortium, including 620,645 parous individuals, among whom 3730 developed incident epithelial ovarian cancer. Using pooled logistic regression models, odds ratios (ORs) and 95% CIs were calculated for the association between breastfeeding and ovarian cancer risk. Ever versus never breastfeeding was associated with a 15% lower risk of ovarian cancer (OR = 0.85, 95% CI = 0.75-0.96), with inverse associations observed for high-grade serous (OR = 0.89, 95% CI = 0.81-0.98) and endometrioid tumors (OR = 0.74, 95% CI = 0.58-0.95). Compared to never breastfeeding, inverse associations were observed for breastfeeding for more than 12 months across total pregnancies (OR = 0.79, 95% CI = 0.68-0.92) as well as for durations of 1-3 months (OR = 0.85, 95% CI = 0.74-0.98). Similar results were observed when stratified by parity. Although risk reduction persisted for up to 30 years since last breastfeeding (OR = 0.81, 95% CI = 0.72-0.91; p-trend < 0.0001), the inverse association was greatest for more recent breastfeeding (OR = 0.56, 95% CI = 0.47-0.66 for < = 20 years). This pooled prospective study provides further evidence that breastfeeding, even for less than 3 months, is associated with lower ovarian cancer risk overall and across most histotypes independent of parity.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Interstage infants with single‐ventricle (SV) physiology following Stage I palliation represent a high‐risk population for noncardiac procedures requiring anesthesia. Data comparing perioperative outcomes by shunt type remain limited. Aims Describe anesthetic management, perioperative complications, and postoperative outcomes in interstage SV infants undergoing noncardiac interventions and compare outcomes between right ventricle‐to‐pulmonary artery (Sano) and modified Blalock‐Taussig‐Thomas shunt (mBTTS) patients. Methods We performed a retrospective single‐center cohort study of interstage SV infants with Stage I palliation undergoing noncardiac surgery or nonsurgical procedures requiring anesthesia between 2015 and 2023. Outcomes were stratified by shunt type. Results A total of 208 noncardiac interventions in 120 interstage SV infants were analyzed; 136 (65.4%) encounters in 86 Sano patients and 72 (34.6%) encounters in 34 mBTTS patients. Compared with mBTTS infants, Sano patients underwent interventions at a younger age (57 [IQR 40–83] vs. 105 [59–278] days, p < 0.001) and lower weight (3.6 [3.0–4.1] vs. 4.8 [3.4–7.3] kg, p < 0.001). mBTTS procedures had higher rates of ventricular dysfunction (34.3% vs. 12.7%, p < 0.001), chromosomal abnormalities (63.9% vs. 19.1%, p < 0.001), gastrointestinal comorbidities (87.5% vs. 72.1%, p = 0.014), and hematologic comorbidities (41.7% vs. 22.8%, p = 0.006). Hemodynamic instability requiring vasoactive support was the most common perioperative complication and occurred similarly between groups (31.9% mBTTS vs. 31.6% Sano, p = 0.962). There were no perioperative cardiac arrests. Rates of postoperative escalation of care (2.9%), reintubation (3.0% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.999), readmission (16.2% vs. 16.9%, p = 0.999), and 30‐day mortality (2.3% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.999) were low and comparable between groups. Conclusions Despite the high‐risk physiology of interstage SV patients, perioperative outcomes were comparable between Sano and mBTTS cohorts. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and should not imply low procedural risk. Favorable outcomes likely reflect careful patient selection, multidisciplinary perioperative care, and specialized institutional expertise.

papers.abstract: Cancer drug resistance remains a principal barrier to durable cancer control, yet it is still often interpreted through endpoint-centred models that emphasise pre-existing resistant clones, incomplete drug exposure or late-acquired mechanisms. These explanations are essential but incomplete. The question is not only why resistant cells exist, but also how residual cells remain alive long enough to become resistant. Across tumour types and therapeutic modalities, treatment reshapes residual populations while it is acting, driving transitions through non-genetic heterogeneity, stochastic cell-fate variability, reversible tolerance, stress adaptation, microenvironmental support and eventually stable resistance. This Review develops a temporal framework in which resistance is resolved into a phase-structured trajectory organised around two mechanistic transitions: entry into adaptive buffering and later stabilisation into resistance hardening. Adaptive buffering is defined operationally as a transient, support-dependent survival state in which residual tumour cells preserve viability by recruiting physiological support systems while molecular and phenotypic reorganisation proceeds. It is not a single pathway or a synonym for drug tolerance, but a functional demand-capacity state whose dependencies change over time. We distinguish adaptive buffering from drug tolerance, persister states, dormancy, minimal residual disease and established resistance and discuss how buffering can be evaluated experimentally using perturbational, single-cell, spatial, computational and functional readouts. The framework suggests that informative biomarkers should assign residual populations to adaptive phases, so that therapy can intercept transient dependencies before adaptive states become hardened and clinically entrenched.

papers.abstract: The erector spinae plane block (ESPB) is widely used for primary breast cancer surgery (BCS), though its clinical benefits within optimized multimodal analgesia pathways remain uncertain. Intravenous lidocaine infusion (IVLI) offers a simple, reproducible alternative with potential systemic analgesic effects. This randomized, tripleblinded, placebo controlled, twocentre trial compared the quality of recovery after ESPB versus IVLI for BCS. Eighty adult patients undergoing primary BCS, with or without axillary dissection, were randomized to receive either ultrasoundguided ESPB (n=40) or intraoperative IVLI (n=40), in addition to a standardized multimodal analgesic protocol. The primary outcome was quality of recovery (QoR15) score at 24 hours. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain scores, opioid consumption, adverse events, and rescue analgesia requirements. Both interventions produced excellent postoperative recovery, with 24hour QoR15 scores approaching preoperative baselines with no significant difference between groups (mean (SD) 24-hour QoR score; ESPB vs. IVLI group, 137.7(17.9) vs. 136.3(8.8), p=0.61). Pain burden and analgesic requirements over the first 24 hours were similarly low, and no ESPB or lidocainerelated adverse events were observed. Within a standardized multimodal analgesic framework, postoperative recovery and analgesic outcomes did not differ significantly between IVLI and ESPB, suggesting that IVLI may offer a pragmatic alternative when regional anesthesia expertise is limited.

papers.abstract: Recovery after non-cardiac surgery increasingly occurs at home, where clinical deterioration may go unrecognized. Digital health interventions may extend postoperative surveillance beyond discharge, but vary widely in components and clinician involvement. We evaluated their association with readmission and other outcomes. Five databases were searched from inception to December 12, 2025, for prospective randomized and observational studies comparing digital health interventions with standard care in adults after non-cardiac surgery. Readmission was the primary outcome; all-cause and major complications, emergency room (ER) visits, length of stay (LOS), and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were secondary. Interventions were grouped by whether a clinician reviewed patient-submitted data and had the ability to take action (active clinician involvement). Random-effects models pooled risk ratios (RR), mean differences (MD), and standardized mean differences (SMD). p values were adjusted for multiple comparisons (Benjamini-Hochberg). In 38 studies (30 randomized, 8 observational; 7,494 patients), digital health interventions were associated with fewer readmissions (17 studies, n=3,944; RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.73-0.99, adjusted p=0.045), ER visits (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.63-0.97), and major complications (RR 0.75, 95% CI 0.60-0.94), but not all-cause complications (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.79-1.08) or LOS (MD -0.04 days, 95% CI -0.26 to 0.18). Pain and anxiety were lower and functional status, quality-of-life, and satisfaction scores higher (absolute SMD 0.41-0.69). Readmission risk was lower with active clinician involvement (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.64-0.92) but not without it (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.78-1.18; interaction p=0.029). Heterogeneity in interventions, cohorts, and outcomes was substantial (PROM I² 50-97%). Digital health interventions were associated with fewer readmissions, ER visits, major complications, and better PROMs, but not fewer all-cause complications or shorter LOS. The readmission association was concentrated in studies with active clinician involvement. Heterogeneity was substantial and certainty of evidence low to very low.

papers.abstract: Abstract B7-H3/CD276 is an emerging immunotherapy target in cancers. However, limited knowledge of B7-H3 signaling and its role in modulating the tumor microenvironment hinders the clinical application of B7-H3–targeting therapy. In this study, we report that B7-H3 plays dual roles in regulating myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSC) and cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAF), thereby promoting tumor progression and therapy resistance, respectively. We comprehensively characterized a noncanonical function of B7-H3 that triggers MAPK signaling in monocytic MDSCs (M-MDSC) and induces cellular senescence. The senescent M-MDSCs secreted chemokines to recruit immunosuppressive granulocytic MDSCs (Gr-MDSC). Genetic deletion or pharmacologic inhibition of B7-H3/CD276 reduced Gr-MDSCs and delayed tumor progression. Nevertheless, the secretory factor SPINK1 derived from MDSCs compensatorily activates EGFR/MEK/ERK signaling in CAFs and promotes their extracellular matrix remodeling features, dampening B7-H3–targeting immunotherapy. Combining the B7-H3 monoclonal antibody with the FDA-approved MEK inhibitor trametinib showed durable antitumor effects in preclinical models of castration-resistant prostate cancer by fully attenuating immunosuppressive mechanisms. Significance: Our studies uncovered a long-unknown B7-H3 signaling that orchestrates the cross-talk of cancer cells with myeloid and stromal cells in the host and provided novel mechanistic insights and effective combinatorial strategies for B7-H3–targeting immunotherapy in advanced prostate cancer among other malignancies.

papers.abstract: Myxopapillary ependymoma (MPE) is an uncommon spinal ependymal tumor that usually arises as a solitary intradural extramedullary (IDEM) lesion in the conus medullaris, cauda equina, or filum terminale. MPE is designated WHO grade 2 since the 2021. Synchronous multifocal spinal MPE at initial presentation is rare and creates uncertainty regarding the extent and timing of surgery. A 34-year-old man with no significant medical history presented with sudden severe non-radicular low-back pain and no neurological deficit. Contrast-enhanced MRI of the brain and entire spine showed multiple enhancing IDEM lesions confined to the lumbosacral region (T12-L1, L2, L3-L4, L4-L5, and S1). The dominant right-sided T12-L1 lesion markedly compressed the conus medullaris/proximal cauda equina. Complete microsurgical resection of this lesion was performed, and histopathology confirmed MPE, WHO grade 2 (Ki-67 ≤ 2-3%). The patient declined radiation-oncology referral, and the remaining lesions were monitored with MRI and CSF cytology, which remained negative. Nine months later, he developed paresthesias and recurrent low-back pain, with enlargement of the L3-L4 and L4-L5 lesions. Both were completely resected in a second operation, while the stable L2 and S1 lesions were left in place. No new neurological deficit occurred after either operation. The patient subsequently underwent radiation-oncology evaluation and received radiotherapy, and the residual lesions were unchanged at 3 months. Multifocal spinal MPE may require individualized, staged management. Prioritizing symptomatic or compressive lesions can achieve decompression and tissue diagnosis while limiting multilevel surgical morbidity. Residual disease warrants long-term imaging surveillance, CSF assessment, and evaluation for radiotherapy.

papers.abstract: Myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDS) are clonal hematopoietic stem cell disorders that frequently progress to secondary acute myeloid leukemia (sAML). Besides intrinsic genetic changes, the disease's development is heavily influenced by the bone marrow (BM) microenvironment, especially mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs). In this study, we present a comprehensive characterization of how unhealthy MSCs affect natural killer (NK) cell anti-leukemic function in MDS and sAML. Using integrated ATAC-seq and RNA-seq profiling, we show that MDS/sAML-derived MSCs induce profound chromatin remodeling in NK cells, marked by reduced promoter accessibility and downregulation of genes essential for stress response and survival. Functionally, pathological MSCs fail to deliver the protective support normally provided by healthy MSCs, instead driving mitochondrial fragmentation and apoptosis in NK cells, ultimately suppressing their cytotoxic activity. Together, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized loss of supportive capacity in pathological MSCs that hampers NK-cell fitness. Therapeutic approaches that bolster mitochondrial resilience in NK cells may help counteract this microenvironment-induced impairment and strengthen immune surveillance in MDS and sAML.

papers.abstract: Recent trials show a survival benefit from adding chemotherapy to endocrine therapy in premenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative node-positive breast cancer. However, whether chemotherapy remains necessary with ovarian function suppression (OFS) is unclear. We retrospectively reviewed patients aged ≤ 50 who underwent surgery (2010-2016) for estrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative, pathologic T1-2N1 breast cancer. Patients were classified by adjuvant treatment received as chemoendocrine therapy (chemotherapy plus tamoxifen with or without OFS; n = 590) or tamoxifen plus OFS (n = 141). Recurrence-free survival (RFS) was compared after 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity score matching (PSM) overall and separately within age groups. Compared with tamoxifen plus OFS, the chemoendocrine group had higher proportions of T2 tumors, greater nodal burden, grade 3 tumors, progesterone receptor-negative disease, and high Ki-67. After PSM, 7-year RFS was 93.6% (95% CI, 89.7-97.7) with chemoendocrine therapy and 90.9% (95% CI, 86.1-96.0) with tamoxifen plus OFS (HR, 1.58; 95% CI, 0.68-3.66; p = 0.28). No significant difference was detected among patients aged 40 years or older (HR, 1.36; 95% CI, 0.47-3.92; p = 0.57), whereas RFS was lower with tamoxifen plus OFS among those younger than 40 years (Firth HR, 13.81; 95% CI, 1.63-1801.17; p = 0.01). The treatment-by-age interaction was not significant (p = 0.63). Overall RFS did not differ significantly after PSM. Although the age-stratified findings remain exploratory, tamoxifen plus OFS may merit further evaluation as a chemotherapy-sparing option in selected patients.

papers.abstract: Despite treatment advances in hormone receptor-positive (HR+) human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 negative (HER2-) metastatic breast cancer (mBC), patients still experience reduced health-related quality of life (HRQoL). This study investigated concordance between patient-physician reported symptoms and side effects, and the impact of reporting on HRQoL among patients with HR+/HER2- mBC. Data were derived from the Adelphi Real World Advanced Breast Cancer Disease Specific Programme (DSP)™, a cross-sectional survey of physicians and their patients with HR+/HER2- mBC receiving treatment, conducted in Europe and the United States between August 2022 and February 2023. Physicians reported patient characteristics, symptoms and side effects. Patients reported symptoms, side-effects and HRQoL using validated instruments. Descriptive, linear regression, and patient-physician concordance analyses were performed. Overall, 298 physicians provided data on 1,642 patients, of which 321 patients self-reported data. Tiredness (85.6%), general worry (75.9%), and worry about future health (75.9%) were the most common patient-reported symptoms and side effects overall. Physicians reported bone pain (30.3%) and appetite changes (13.2%) as the most frequent patient symptoms, while estimating that most patients experienced no side effects (55.1%). Concordance between patient-physician symptom reporting was generally low (kappa ≤ 0.20), with higher concordance associated with better HRQoL across multiple measures (p < 0.001). Patients with HR+/HER2- mBC experience substantial disease and treatment-mediated side effects, with low patient-physician concordance associated with worse HRQoL. These results underscore the value of capturing patient-reported experiences to better characterize symptom burden and quality of life. Not applicable.

papers.abstract: Progestogen-associated intracranial meningiomas are increasingly recognized as a distinct clinical entity, often characterized by multiplicity and preferential skull-base location. However, epilepsy in this population remains poorly characterized. We aimed to assess the prevalence, clinical features, and factors associated with epilepsy in women with progestogen-associated meningiomas. We retrospectively analyzed consecutive adult women managed for intracranial meningioma at a tertiary neuro-oncology center between 2000 and 2024, with documented exposure to at least one progestogen associated with increased meningioma risk and available clinical and imaging data. Epilepsy was analyzed at the patient level using one index meningioma per patient. Given the low number of epilepsy events, analyses were descriptive. A total of 209 women were included (mean age 51.9 ± 10.1 years), including 69 (33.0%) with multiple meningiomas. Epilepsy at diagnosis occurred in 4.8% of patients and in 13.3% of symptomatic patients. Patients with epilepsy had larger index meningiomas than those without (24.6±24.3 vs 8.8 ± 16.9 cm3), more frequent meningioma-related brain edema (70.0% vs 19.1%), and more frequent midline mass effect (60.0% vs 13.6%). No association was detected with progestogen type or exposure pattern. Following antiseizure medication initiation, seizures were controlled in all patients with epilepsy at diagnosis. At last follow-up, seizures were controlled in 7/9 (77.8%) evaluable patients. During follow-up, de novo epilepsy remained uncommon, particularly among patients initially managed conservatively. Epilepsy is uncommon in women with progestogen-associated intracranial meningiomas. When present, it appears to be primarily related to tumor burden and meningioma-brain interface involvement, whereas no association with specific progestogen exposure characteristics was detected.

papers.abstract: Many patients undergoing neoadjuvant therapy for localized pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) experience treatment intolerance or disease progression during initial therapy. Although chemotherapy switch is increasingly utilized, response rates and oncologic outcomes remain poorly defined. Patients were identified from a prospectively maintained database of individuals undergoing neoadjuvant therapy for localized PDAC from 2012 to 2023. Eligible patients underwent chemotherapy switch between 5-fluorouracil and gemcitabine regimens with curative intent. Favorable response was defined as complete or partial radiographic response by RECIST, or stable disease with a ≥ 50% decline in CA 19-9 relative to levels before switch. Outcomes were measured from the date of chemotherapy switch. Out of 161 patients, 41% achieved favorable response. Body/tail, borderline resectable, and locally advanced disease were independently associated with nonfavorable response. Among favorable responders, 49% underwent resection versus 11% of nonresponders. Favorable response was independently associated with improved progression-free and overall survival, including among unresected patients. Overall, 47% derived meaningful oncologic benefit through favorable response, resection, or both. Chemotherapy switch offers a reasonable strategy in select patients with localized PDAC experiencing inadequate response or intolerance of initial therapy. This composite response framework identifies chemosensitive tumor biology, informs surgical decision-making, and stratifies prognosis.

papers.abstract: Microscopic margin involvement (≤ 1 mm) strongly predicts poor prognosis in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) after upfront resection fails to fully mitigate this risk. It remains uncertain whether neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) can neutralize the adverse prognostic impact of impending ≤ 1 mm margins. Prognostic significance of ≤ 1 mm margins was assessed in an upfront-resection cohort (n = 228) using multivariable Cox regression. A separate cohort (n = 110; 52 NACT, 58 upfront surgery) compared overall survival (OS) by margin status. A CT-based radiomics model using a Laplacian-Dirichlet operator was developed to predict ≤ 1 mm margins and externally validated (n = 230). ≤ 1 mm margins independently predicted worse OS vs. > 1 mm (15.0 vs. 24.0 months, p = 0.005). ACT numerically extended OS for ≤ 1 mm patients (16.0 vs. 15.0 months, p = 0.271) but did not close the survival gap. Notably, ≤ 1 mm patients receiving NACT achieved median OS of 29.4 months-comparable to > 1 mm upfront patients (31.6 months)-and significantly better than ≤ 1 mm upfront patients (19.6 months, p = 0.045). The model predicted ≤ 1 mm margins with AUCs of 0.772 (95% CI: 0.705-0.838) and 0.723 (95% CI: 0.657-0.789) in internal and external validation. NACT-not ACT-selectively rescues high-risk patients destined for ≤ 1 mm margins. Our radiomics model enables preoperative identification, supporting personalized neoadjuvant therapy.

papers.abstract: Postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF) remains a significant source of morbidity following pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD), and whether internal or external stenting better mitigates POPF after robotic PD (RPD) remains unclear. A retrospective review was conducted of patients who underwent RPD with internalized or externalized pancreatic duct stents at a single academic institution (2020-2026). POPF was graded by ISGPS criteria, with risk stratified by Fistula Risk Score (FRS) and Alternative FRS (A-FRS). Ninety-day outcomes were recorded. Of 182 patients, 83 (45.6%) received an externalized stent. Age, sex, BMI, and PDAC proportion were similar between internal and external stent groups, as was fistula risk (74.7% vs. 71.1% intermediate/high risk) (all p > 0.05). Overall POPF rate was nearly identical (18.2% vs. 18.1%; p = 0.985), with most fistulas (73.5%) being biochemical leaks and no Grade C fistulas. Among low/intermediate A-FRS patients, clinically-relevant POPF rates were comparable (2.6% vs. 2.9%; p = 0.994). In high A-FRS patients, external stenting was associated with significantly fewer clinically-relevant POPFs (0.0% vs. 21.7%) and more biochemical leaks (35.7% vs. 8.7%, p = 0.04). External stenting did not increase length of stay or readmission. In high fistula-risk RPD patients, external stenting was associated with fewer clinically-relevant POPFs, suggesting externalization may prevent progression to clinically-relevant POPF.

papers.abstract: The role of the human microbiome in cancer development, progression, and response to therapy has moved from correlative curiosity to demonstrated impact on tumor biology. This represents a critical factor for surgical oncologists as they not only resect these tumors, but also direct perioperative antimicrobial exposure and increasingly co-manage neoadjuvant and surveillance pathways in which microbial state may predict and modify response. This review summarizes the basis for therapeutic modulation of the cancer microbiome and metabolome in a contemporary clinical-trial landscape across four broad strategies: additive (fecal microbiota transplantation, defined consortia, and live biotherapeutic products), subtractive (targeted antimicrobials), dietary and metabolome-directed interventions, and engineered or next-generation platforms. Particular attention is given to subtractive approaches in colon and rectal cancer and to the underexplored perioperative interface between the microbiome and surgical outcomes such as anastomotic leak. We outline the principal methodological and translational obstacles, including low-biomass contamination, causal inference, unintended antibiotic effects, and product standardization. Looking ahead, we propose roles for surgeons across the care continuum, from biospecimen stewardship and trial referral to integration of microbiome and circulating tumor DNA signals in surveillance.

papers.abstract: Fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma (FL-HCC) is a rare liver malignancy affecting predominantly young patients, though management can differ between pediatric and adult populations. We evaluated age-related differences in treatment and overall survival (OS). Patients with FL-HCC diagnosed from 2004 to 2021 were identified in the National Cancer Database. Demographic, tumor, and treatment characteristics were compared, and OS was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Among 487 patients, 172 were children (< 18 years) and 315 were adults (≥ 18 years). Children more frequently underwent lymph node removal (80.0% vs 58.6%) and had higher positive-margin rates (15.1% vs 6.7%). Five-year OS was 70.5% in children versus 61.6% in adults. On multivariable analysis, adulthood (HR 1.38, 95% CI 1.00-1.89), metastasis at diagnosis (HR 3.47, 95% CI 2.39-5.02), and positive margins (HR 3.16, 95% CI 2.15-4.64) were associated with increased mortality. Pediatric patients with FL-HCC had superior OS despite similar disease burden. Positive margins were strongly associated with mortality, supporting efforts to achieve R0 resection.

papers.abstract: Count-based nodal staging classifies periampullary and pancreatic head carcinoma by the number of involved nodes. Because extranodal extension (ENE) occurs only in node-positive disease, its prognostic value must be judged against node-positive patients without ENE. We examined whether ENE adds prognostic information beyond nodal count among node-positive patients after pancreatoduodenectomy. We analysed 304 consecutive pancreatoduodenectomies (October 2019-May 2025; median lymph node yield 24). The primary analysis was restricted to node-positive patients (n = 125), with node-positive ENE-negative patients as reference, using Cox regression adjusted for N2 versus N1, perineural invasion, age and pancreatic head primary. Sensitivity analyses added pathological covariates and adjuvant therapy, applied a 90-day landmark, and excluded non-adenocarcinoma histology. ENE was identified in 26 patients (8.6%), constituting 20.8% of node-positive cases. Among node-positive patients, 2-year overall survival was 55.2% with ENE versus 80.1% without (log-rank p < 0.001). ENE was independently associated with mortality (HR 3.23, 95% CI 1.56-6.67; p = 0.002), whereas N2 versus N1 (HR 1.15; p = 0.69) and perineural invasion (HR 1.00; p = 0.99) were not. The association persisted in all sensitivity analyses (HR range 2.49-3.14), including the 90-day landmark (HR 2.97) and adenocarcinoma-only (HR 2.49) cohorts. Among node-positive patients, ENE was associated with survival beyond nodal count. These findings are hypothesis-generating; they support routine synoptic reporting of ENE and warrant multi-centre validation before any staging implication is considered.

papers.abstract: Little is known about the outcomes of patients with gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEA) who respond poorly to neoadjuvant FLOT (5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, docetaxel) on imaging. We aimed to determine whether imaging non-response to FLOT was associated with worse pathologic features, recurrence patterns, and survival outcomes. Patients with GEA who received neoadjuvant FLOT from January 2017 to April 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Staging and re-staging computed tomography and positron emission tomography were used to determine tumor response, stratifying the cohort into FLOT responders or non-responders (FNRs). Pathologic features, overall survival (OS) and event-free survival (EFS) were compared between the two groups. Survival data from 193 patients were analyzed: 116 (60.1%) were responders and 77 (39.9%) were FNR; 24 patients in the FNR group developed metastases and were not included in pathologic analysis (n = 169). FNRs had worse performance status, more advanced ypT and ypN stage, less pathologic tumor regression, and higher rates of lymphovascular and perineural invasion than responders. Imaging response to FLOT was significantly associated with pathologic tumor regression grade (p < 0.001). Median OS was lower in the FNR group (24.6 vs. 67 months, log rank p < 0.001), as was median EFS (13 vs. 32 months, log rank p < 0.001). FLOT non-response was a prognostic factor for OS (hazard ratio 1.989; 95% confidence interval 1.079-3.669; p = 0.028) on multivariable analysis. In the 81 patients who experienced recurrence after resection, there was no difference in OS and EFS with imaging response. Patients with GEA with poor response to FLOT on imaging demonstrated significantly worse pathologic features and OS and EFS.

papers.abstract: Complete resection is central to curative-intent treatment of primary gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumors. Although minimally invasive surgery (MIS) is appealing, evidence for robotic resection of large or anatomically difficult tumors remains limited. We retrospectively reviewed patients undergoing resection of primary gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumors at the Mayo Clinic, Rochester (2010-2025). Demographics, operative details, pathology, and outcomes were summarized descriptively. Recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods. Among 263 patients, the median tumor size was 4.0 cm; 31% exceeded 5 cm. Laparoscopy was used in 42.2%, open surgery in 30.0%, and robotics in 27.8%, with robotic use increasing over time and predominating by 2025. Wedge resection was most common (79.8%), followed by transgastric resection (15.9%); intraoperative endoscopy was used in 40.6%. R0 resection was achieved in 97.7%, with no intraoperative tumor ruptures and a 3.3% conversion rate among MIS cases. In the analytic cohort (n = 173), MIS was used for 75.5% of tumors > 5 cm and all cardia tumors and was associated with lower blood loss and shorter hospital stay. Median RFS and OS were not reached; 5-year RFS and OS were 78.1 and 85.0%. RFS differed by tumor grade (p = 0.009). Among MIS resections of tumors > 5 cm (n = 40), R0 was 97.5%, with no conversions or ruptures; R0 reached 100% for cardia/gastroesophageal junction/incisura tumors (n = 15). Anatomic gastrectomy was avoided in 86% of MIS cases. Outcomes depended more on patient selection and tailored technique than operative platform. MIS, including robotics, enabled safe, margin-negative resection with rapid recovery, whereas RFS reflected tumor biology.

papers.abstract: A minimally invasive approach currently is the gold standard for distal pancreatectomy (DP). Robotic distal pancreatectomy (RDP) is increasingly adopted and offers technical advantages. As life expectancy rises, more octogenarians undergo pancreatic resection, and emerging evidence suggests minimally invasive approaches may benefit older adults. However, the role of RDP in this population remains underexplored. A multi-institutional retrospective cohort study from four high-volume North American hepato-pancreatobiliary centers was conducted. Adults undergoing elective open distal pancreatectomy (ODP) or RDP between 2007 and 2023 were stratified as < 80 versus ≥ 80 years of age. The primary outcome was 90-day mortality. The secondary outcomes included major complications and oncologic outcomes. Multivariable models were applied to adjust for relevant covariates. A subanalysis was performed on patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Of 797 patients undergoing DP, 62 were aged ≥ 80 years. Despite more comorbidities and higher PDAC rates, older patients had comparable perioperative outcomes. Blood loss, conversion, complications, length of stay, readmissions, and 90-day mortality were similar between age groups. On adjusted analysis, age ≥ 80 years was not associated with major complications or 90-day mortality in the overall cohort or PDAC subgroup. Whereas RDP was independently associated with fewer major complications, longer operative time and greater blood loss increased adverse outcomes. Among PDAC patients, perioperative and oncologic outcomes, including survival, were comparable across age groups. Octogenarians achieve perioperative and oncologic outcomes comparable with those of younger patients when treated in high-volume centers, including survival. A robotic approach proved advantageous in reducing complications. The current findings reinforce the role of resection when indicated.

papers.abstract: Fatigue is a common, multidimensional symptom in cancer patients. Little is known about fatigue dimensions and their trajectories in prostate cancer (PCa). Using the Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI), 1097 men treated with radiotherapy for non-metastatic PCa (2014-2016) prospectively reported fatigue up to five years later. Prevalent fatigue was defined as scores ≥75th percentile in men aged ≥60 years in a German general population sample. Pre-radiotherapy patient characteristics were examined for their associations with general fatigue, physical fatigue, mental fatigue, reduced activity, and reduced motivation two years later using logistic regression models. Fatigue trajectories up to two years post-radiotherapy were explored using latent class growth analysis and multinomial regression. About 72% (785/1097) of patients reported being fatigued for at least one dimension in the MFI from before the start of radiotherapy up to five years later, with 45% (367/816) being fatigued two years post-radiotherapy. Pre-radiotherapy fatigue level (OR: 4.7-9.0), depression (OR: 2.5), diabetes (OR: 1.8-2.2), hypertension (OR: 1.6-1.8), and BMI (OR: 1.8-2.2) were statistically significant predictors of long-term fatigue two years post-radiotherapy across dimensions. Depression, BMI, and pelvic radiotherapy were associated with experiencing a high fatigue trajectory. Early fatigue assessments, in addition to self-reported comorbidities and BMI, showed additional benefits beyond symptom detection by providing prognostic value for poorer long-term fatigue outcomes. Multidimensional fatigue assessments could guide tailored symptom management strategies, targeting specific dimensions to address associated impairments in quality of life and functioning.

papers.abstract: Dose-dense adjuvant chemotherapy prolongs survival in breast cancer and has been translated into neoadjuvant settings. Although weekly nanoparticle albumin-bound (nab)-paclitaxel yields superior pathological complete response (pCR) rates relative to solvent-based paclitaxel, data supporting its incorporation into a dose-dense neoadjuvant regimen-particularly for hormone receptor positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 negative (HR+/HER2-) tumours-remain limited. This trial therefore evaluated whether a bi-weekly dose-dense nab-paclitaxel schedule improves the proportion of residual cancer burden (RCB) 0/Ⅰ compared with a comparable dose-dense docetaxel regimen, each followed by dose-dense epirubicin plus cyclophosphamide. This was a multicentre, randomised, phase III trial done at three hospitals in China. HR⁺/HER2⁻ patients (cT1-3/N0-1/M0) were randomised 1:1 using dynamic allocation with Pocock minimisation on Ki-67 and TNM stage. The experimental arm received nab-paclitaxel 260 mg/m² intravenously on day 1 every two weeks for four cycles; the control arm received docetaxel 100 mg/m² on the identical schedule. Both cohorts subsequently received epirubicin 90 mg/m² plus cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² intravenously on day 1 every two weeks for four cycles. Primary endpoints were RCB 0/Ⅰ rate; secondary endpoints encompassed disease free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. Between December 2019 and December 2020, 388 patients (194 per arm) were enrolled. The nab-paclitaxel arm attained an RCB 0/Ⅰ rate of 20.1% (95% CI 14.41-26.72), significantly exceeding the docetaxel arm's 11.34% (95% CI 6.92-15.81; χ²=5.62, P = 0.018). pCR was achieved in 15.98% (95% CI 10.81-21.16) of the nab-paclitaxel group versus 10.31% (95% CI 6.01-14.60) of the docetaxel group (χ²=2.73, P = 0.098). Multivariate analysis confirmed a statistically significant favourable impact of nab-paclitaxel on RCB 0/Ⅰ. Five-year DFS was comparable (90.21% vs. 87.11%; HR: 1.14, 95% CI 0.64-2.05; P = 0.656), as was five-year OS (96.34% vs. 95.31%; HR: 0.64, 95% CI 0.29-1.42; P = 0.274), indicating no significant survival disparity. Grade 3/4 adverse event incidence was similar (30% vs. 38%). The most frequent all-grade toxicities (neutropenia, nausea, myalgia) occurred at comparable rates; however, grade 3/4 peripheral sensory neuropathy was observed exclusively in the nab-paclitaxel cohort. No treatment-related mortality was reported. A bi-weekly dose-dense nab-paclitaxel regimen followed by dose-dense epirubicin-cyclophosphamide constitutes a feasible and efficacious neoadjuvant strategy for early stage HR+/HER2- breast cancer, delivering a higher RCB 0/Ⅰ rate without compromising overall safety. The increased incidence of high-grade peripheral neuropathy mandates vigilant monitoring, yet the regimen represents a valuable addition to contemporary neoadjuvant options.
