papers.abstract: HER2-positive breast cancer is a distinct subtype associated with less favorable outcomes without targeted therapy. Dual HER2 blockade with pertuzumab and trastuzumab has shown improved efficacy compared to single-agent approaches, but results across studies remain variable. This meta-analysis aims to evaluate the overall efficacy and safety of pertuzumab-based regimens. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library was conducted to identify relevant RCTs. The quality of trials was assessed using the ROB-2 tool, and the certainty of the evidence was assessed using the GRADE tool. Data were synthesized using R. This study included 8 RCTs with 8367 patients. Pertuzumab-based regimens were associated with improved overall survival. In the locally advanced or metastatic setting, a pronounced benefit was observed (HR = 0.71, 95% CI 0.65-0.77). However, in the neoadjuvant or adjuvant setting, the pooled hazard ratio (HR = 0.81, 95% CI 0.22-3.04), which was not significant. Progression-free survival (HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.67-0.83) was improved compared with the control group. In terms of safety, there was no significant difference in the incidence of any adverse events (risk ratio (RR) = 1.01; 95% CI 0.99-1.02) or grade ≥ 3 adverse events (RR 0.99; 95% CI 0.86-1.13) between the experimental and control groups. Pertuzumab-based dual HER2 blockade is associated with significant improvements in overall survival and progression-free survival in patients with metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer. Importantly, these survival benefits are not accompanied by a significant increase in overall or severe adverse events, supporting its favorable efficacy-safety profile across clinical settings.

papers.abstract: Disease recurrence after definitive therapy remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality in early-stage breast cancer, with limited options for treatment intensification. Cell surface-targeted (CST) therapies, including antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), radiopharmaceuticals, and immune-based approaches, have demonstrated success in treating malignancies. However, the known CST repertoire in breast cancer is narrow, largely restricted to HER2 and TROP2, highlighting an unmet need for novel targets in treatment-resistant disease. We profiled CST expression using large-scale gene expression datasets annotated with clinical outcomes, including SCAN-B (n ≈ 10,000), aggregated neoadjuvant chemotherapy cohorts (n ≈ 4,000), and the randomized SWEBCG91RT trial (n = 765). CSTs with therapies in clinical trials were prioritized. RNA-protein correlation was assessed using CPTAC and SCMP datasets. Associations with recurrence-free survival (RFS) and treatment response were analyzed using Cox regression and Fisher's exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Of 78 CSTs under active clinical investigation, RNA expression strongly predicted protein expression (median accuracy 80-94%). In ER+ breast cancer treated with endocrine therapy, nine CSTs (including CEACAM5/6, EPCAM, NECTIN4) were associated with significantly worse RFS. Of these, EPCAM and CEACAM5 were also associated with poor outcomes specifically after radiotherapy in the SWEBCG91RT trial. In HER2 + disease, high expression of FOLH1 and TNFRSF10B predicted relapse despite anti-HER2 therapy. In triple-negative breast cancer, six CSTs were associated with residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy. These analyses identify potential candidates for repositioning CST drugs, and single-cell analysis revealed substantial intratumoral heterogeneity for several targets, informing payload selection strategies. CSTs associated with treatment resistance across breast cancer subtypes represent actionable opportunities for therapeutic repositioning. These findings provide a framework for rational integration of CST therapies in early-stage breast cancer.

papers.abstract: Paratracheal air cysts are rare benign anatomical variants. Although case reports suggest that paratracheal air cysts may lead to complications such as difficult ventilation and pneumothorax in patients whose lungs are mechanically ventilated, their association with postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) remains unclear. We hypothesized that the presence of cysts is associated with an increased incidence of PPCs. In the context of COVID-19, we conducted a retrospective study of all patients undergoing surgery under general anesthesia in 2020. On the basis of the presence of paratracheal air cysts, we divided patients into two groups: the paratracheal air cyst group and the paratracheal-air-cyst‑free group. The primary outcome was the incidence of PPCs. We used propensity score matching to adjust for confounding and performed multivariable logistic regression analysis in the matched cohort to assess the association. Among 7,208 patients, the prevalence of paratracheal air cysts was 2.0% (141/7,208). The incidence of PPCs was 22% (31/141) in the paratracheal air cyst group and 15% (43/280) in the paratracheal-air-cyst-free group. Multivariable regression analysis showed that, after adjusting for confounders, the presence of paratracheal air cysts was associated with an increased risk of PPCs (adjusted odds ratio, 1.85; 95% confidence interval, 1.03 to 3.33; P = 0.04). The presence of paratracheal air cysts was associated with an increased risk of PPCs. Although this association warrants cautious interpretation due to possible residual confounding and lack of data on intraoperative ventilatory settings, anesthesiologists should consider the potential perioperative implications of this anatomical abnormality during preoperative assessment.

papers.abstract: Given the fiduciary responsibility of an academic clinical department to ensure appropriate use of funds to support research, the Department of Anesthesia, Pain Management and Perioperative Medicine at Dalhousie University (Halifax, NS, Canada) aimed to create a framework to support the allocation of remunerated protected research time to clinician faculty members within the department. A departmental Research Accountability Project (RAP) was undertaken in the context of a quality improvement initiative. The RAP initially engaged clinician faculty members in the form of a survey, interviews, and a questionnaire to provide feedback regarding current practices for evaluating protected time for research. On the basis of this feedback, a working group created a list of 151 research outputs encompassing the breadth of research-related activities and assigned scores based on their relative merit. Clinicians with protected research time completed their academic profile, and individual point allocations were calculated. Scores were then weighted by different categories (e.g., publications, grant capture, presentations), and a RAP dashboard was developed to capture research outputs, assign scores, and generate a reporting/feedback mechanism for further analysis. Faculty members acknowledged the importance of clinicians having remunerated protected time to carry out research; nevertheless, there was scepticism with respect to how protected research time was managed. These data were then assessed by the working group, and using the RAP metric, individual researcher reports consisting of scores and recommendations were sent to the department head for final evaluation. These reports formed the basis of the researchers' annual academic performance review and consideration for continuance. The RAP scoring system provides an objective measure of remunerated protected research time for clinicians to assist in researcher accountability.

papers.abstract: Incretin mimetics as obesity therapy induce substantial weight and fat loss but also decrease lean soft tissue mass, possibly impairing skeletal muscle function. Here, in this two-arm randomized controlled trial of adding resistance exercise (REx) to tirzepatide (T), 120 adults with overweight or obesity were treated with tirzepatide and randomized to thrice-weekly resistance exercise training or usual activities for 40 weeks. Tirzepatide was safe, and most participants tolerated up-titration to 15 mg weekly. Adherence to resistance exercise was 91%. Weight loss achieved was similar (T = -22.61 kg, T+REx = -22.28 kg, P = 0.694). For primary outcomes, loss of total fat mass was similar (T = -17.19 kg, T+REx = -17.98 kg, P = 0.700; between-group difference = -0.77 kg, 95% confidence interval (CI): -2.14 kg to 0.60 kg), but resistance exercise reduced loss of total lean soft tissue mass (T = -4.67 kg, T+REx = -3.57 kg, P < 0.001; between-group difference = 1.09 kg, 95% CI: 0.43-1.75 kg). For related endpoints, resistance exercise reduced loss of appendicular lean soft tissue mass (T = -3.55 kg, T+REx = -2.92 kg, P < 0.001). Upper and lower body muscle strength decreased with tirzepatide (bench press -4.09 kg, lat pulldown -4.42 kg, knee extension -4.42 kg) but increased with T+REx (+4.68 kg, +8.58 kg, +5.88 kg, respectively, all P < 0.001 versus tirzepatide). In conclusion, resistance exercise training attenuated loss of total lean soft tissue mass, representing an effective adjunct to tirzepatide anti-obesity therapy. papers.abstract: Predicting difficult intubation is still challenging, even with videolaryngoscopy. Videolaryngoscopy (VL) shows the larynx during intubation. The modified Cormack-Lehane (CL) classification grades laryngeal visibility but can vary between observers. Deep learning uses neural networks for objective, real-time airway image evaluation. We aimed to evaluate a YOLOv8-based model for object detection to automate modified CL grade classification from VL images in patients undergoing elective surgery. In this prospective observational study, we developed a deep learning model using 346 VL images from 151 patients undergoing elective surgery. Two anesthesiologists classified images according to the modified CL system, and interobserver agreement was analysed using Cohen's kappa and weighted kappa. We split the data into training (80%), validation (10%), and test (10%) sets, with imbalance corrected via Albumentations augmentation. We evaluated the model results using sensitivity, specificity, and mean average precision with a 95% confidence interval (CI) and validated the model on 60 images not included in the training set. Interobserver agreement ranged from moderate (Cohen's kappa = 0.59; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.66) to good (weighted kappa = 0.79; 95% CI, 0.75 to 0.84). In the test set, the overall recall rate was 0.87, and the specificity was 0.83. In the difficult intubation grades, recall and specificity were observed to be 0.79 (95% CI, 0.52 to 0.92) and 0.93 (95% CI, 0.78 to 0.98), respectively, for CL grade 2b, and 0.60 and 1.00, respectively, for CL grade 3. In the external validation data set (n = 60), the model achieved an overall accuracy of 0.767 with a recognition rate of 0.925 for clinically relevant CL grades 2b and 3. The YOLOv8-based model showed promising performance in classifying modified CL grades, particularly for clinically relevant difficult views (CL grades 2b-3). Nevertheless, wide CIs and limited external validation indicate uncertainty. The model may be considered an auxiliary tool rather than an independent decision system and requires further validation in larger, multicentre data sets.

papers.abstract: The management of malignant bone sarcomas in the lower extremities of skeletally immature children and adolescents remains a major challenge in orthopedic oncology. Expandable endoprostheses have become more popular over the last decades, but scientific data are limited. To provide reliable data on functional outcomes, complications, and survival rates after this procedure, we conducted a systematic literature review and meta-analysis of prospective and retrospective studies. The primary objective was Musculoskeletal Tumor Society functional score. Secondary objectives included complications and survival rates. Risk of bias was assessed using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS) tool. A total of 1055 patients from 27 studies met the eligibility criteria. Overall methodological quality was moderate, with a mean MINORS score of 10.44. The mean age at surgery was 10.0 years (range 2.0-16.0), and the median follow-up was 5.44 years (range 1.7-24.0). Osteosarcoma accounted for 88.0% of cases and Ewing sarcoma for 10.4%. The pooled estimate of Musculoskeletal Tumor Society score was 82.9 (95% confidence interval [CI] 80.5-85.3). The pooled complication rate was 58.0% (95% CI 48.0-67.0), with no significant difference between minimally invasive and non-invasive expansion mechanisms. According to the Henderson/International Society of Limb Salvage classification, type III structural failures were the most frequent failure mode in both minimally invasive and non-invasive cohorts. The pooled 5-year overall survival rate was 76.0% (95% CI 54.7-89.2). This meta-analysis supports expandable endoprostheses as an effective limb-salvage option for skeletally immature patients with bone sarcoma, providing good functional outcomes and acceptable 5-year survival despite a high complication burden.

papers.abstract: A barrier to precision medicine for ulcerative colitis (UC) is the inability to predict and mechanistically explain treatment responses. Using patient-reported outcomes (PROs) from a phase 3b comparative trial of 768 participants, we identified four distinct patient response-trajectory groups for vedolizumab (anti-integrin) and adalimumab (antitumor necrosis factor). Validation in a second phase 3 trial of 576 participants linked PRO-defined vedolizumab trajectories to long-term disease complications. Bulk, single cell, and spatial transcriptomics and proteomics identified vascular inflammation as associated with vedolizumab nonresponse through interactions between SPP1+ macrophages and endothelial cells. In two separate real-world cohorts of 4,981 and 3,854 patients with UC, concomitant use of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (modulators of vascular inflammation) was associated with reduced long-term complications for vedolizumab but not anticytokine therapies. These findings define a response-trajectory-based taxonomy that requires prospective validation for clinical utility and applications for selecting vedolizumab combination therapy in UC.

papers.abstract: We report clinical outcomes, mutation testing patterns, and treatment patterns from a global, real-world, retrospective, observational study in patients with stage 1/2 epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Data were extracted from medical records of adults with stage 1/2 EGFR-mutated NSCLC (diagnosed January 2016-December 2019), who underwent stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) as standard of care. The primary objective was assessment of real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS). Secondary objectives included assessment of mutation testing patterns, treatment sequencing post-SBRT, real-world time to next treatment or death (rwTTNTD), and real-world overall survival (rwOS). Data were extracted from medical records of 82 patients across six countries; 66% of patients had medically inoperable tumors; 43% had tumors harboring exon 19 deletion (Ex19del), 55% had L858R, 1% had both Ex19del and L858R, and 1% had L858R and an exon 20 insertion. Overall, 91% of patients had stage 1A/1B disease and 9% had stage 2A/2B. All patients underwent SBRT as standard of care; 31 patients (38%) progressed following SBRT. Of patients who received subsequent treatment (n = 25), most received EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs; 88%; n = 22/25); first-/second-generation EGFR-TKIs n=17, third-generation EGFR-TKIs n=5. Median (95% confidence interval [CI]) rwPFS, rwTTNTD, and rwOS were 47.1 (38.7-57.8), 49.8 (40.7-not estimable [NE]), and 62.9 (50.8-NE) months, respectively. The rwPFS rates at 12, 24, 36, 48, and 60 months (95% CI) were 90% (81-95), 76% (65-84), 65% (53-74), 48% (35-60), and 34% (19-48), respectively. In this global, real-world, retrospective study in patients with stage 1/2 EGFR-mutated NSCLC who underwent SBRT, the majority of whom had medically inoperable tumors, the 4-year rwPFS rate was <50%. Further studies are needed to confirm the potential role for EGFR-TKI therapy in this setting.

papers.abstract: Accurate segmentation of clinical target volumes (CTV) is critical for the success of radiotherapy in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Manual contouring is time-consuming and prone to considerable inter-observer variability. Current auto-segmentation models rely exclusively on images, which may lead to sub-optimal accuracy. This study sought to substantially improve CTV auto-segmentation by incorporating tumor and clinical text information with multimodal deep learning. We retrospectively collected data from 184 NPC patients treated at our institution, with 144 cases allocated for model training and 40 for test. We propose a tumor- and text-aware multi-view UMamba (TTA-MVUM) model with text-image cross-attention modules to fuse visual and textual features. The model input comprised CT images, manually contoured primary gross tumor volume and metastatic lymph nodes, structured text contouring plan extracted by a large language model from electronic health records. Training was guided by a composite loss integrating Dice, cross-entropy and contrastive terms. Model performance was evaluated using Dice, 95% Hausdorff distance and averaged surface distance. The proposed TTA-MVUM model significantly outperformed state-of-the-art image-only and tumor-aware baselines, yielding mean Dice of 0.892 ± 0.035 for high-risk CTV, 0.738 ± 0.149 for low-risk CTV, and 0.889 ± 0.024 for the entire CTV, respectively, with similar improvements for other metrics. Using either tumor information or clinical text alone also surpassed baseline models, but performance remained inferior to the combined approach. Integrating tumor priors and text guidance can substantially improve the NPC CTV auto-segmentation accuracy and clinical applicability.

papers.abstract: Osimertinib is a third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor that has become a mainstay treatment for EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, acquired resistance develops in most patients and ultimately compromises durable clinical benefit. Therefore, effective combination strategies to enhance Osimertinib sensitivity and delay or overcome resistance remain an urgent unmet clinical need. The antitumor effects of pterostilbene in combination with Osimertinib were evaluated in EGFR-mutant and osimertinib-resistant NSCLC cell lines using CCK-8, colony formation, EdU incorporation, wound healing, and Transwell invasion assays. In vivo efficacy and safety were evaluated in nude mouse xenograft models. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, ferroptosis-related biochemical parameters, protein expression profiles, and transcriptomic profiles were analyzed. The involvement of ferroptosis and FGFR4 signaling was further validated using the ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) and FGFR4 siRNA-mediated knockdown. Pterostilbene markedly potentiated the antitumor efficacy of Osimertinib in vitro and in vivo and restored drug responsiveness in Osimertinib-resistant NSCLC cells. Mechanistically, the combination induced ferroptosis, as indicated by enhanced lipid peroxidation, intracellular Fe2+ accumulation, and reduced expression of key ferroptosis-protective proteins, including GPX4 and xCT. Consistently, pharmacological inhibition of ferroptosis attenuated the antitumor effects of the combination. Furthermore, combined treatment modulated FGFR4-associated ERK/AKT signaling and disrupted redox and iron homeostasis. FGFR4 depletion significantly attenuated ferroptosis induction and reduced the synergistic anticancer effects of the combination, whereas FGFR4 re-expression restored treatment responsiveness, supporting an FGFR4-dependent therapeutic response. This study demonstrates that pterostilbene enhances the antitumor efficacy of Osimertinib through the induction of FGFR4-dependent ferroptosis, providing mechanistic insights and suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy to overcome EGFR-TKI resistance in NSCLC.

papers.abstract: Previous reviews have described disparities in the treatment of patients diagnosed with gynecologic cancers; however, these reviews are not systematic in nature, and none have focused specifically on individuals diagnosed with cervical cancer, who disproportionately represent marginalized populations in the US. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on treatment-related outcomes and multilevel determinants of care among US patients with cervical cancer. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42023413020). We searched PubMed, Scopus, and CINAHL for studies published through May 2026. Eligible studies examined treatment related outcomes among patients diagnosed with cervical cancer in the US. We identified 25 articles that met our inclusion criteria. Treatment-related outcomes were categorized and determinants (i.e., explanatory variables) were mapped on to the socioecological model. Across 25 studies, 26 treatment-related outcomes were identified. Receipt of surgery, chemotherapy, and brachytherapy were the most frequently assessed outcomes. Key patient-level determinants included race/ethnicity, age, comorbidities, insurance, rurality, and distance to care. Minoritized populations, particularly Black, Hispanic, Native American, Pacific Islander, often experienced worse treatment outcomes. Older age was also a frequent barrier to treatment. Distance to care was inconsistently associated with treatment outcomes. Clinic-level determinants, such as care outside of large-volume facilities and academic medical centers, and contextual determinants, such as residing in a county with lower levels of income and education, were associated with worse treatment outcomes. Cervical cancer treatment in the United States is driven by multilevel determinants at the patient-, clinic-, and community-level. Addressing barriers to treatment requires attention to the broader structural and modifiable factors that hinder treatment for marginalized cervical cancer patients in vulnerable communities. Future studies should more rigorously and thoughtfully measure community-level and individual-level variables.

papers.abstract: Cellular senescence acts as a core driver of chronic diseases and tissue degeneration. Conventional small-molecule senolytics face critical limitations including poor target specificity and off-target toxicity when eliminating heterogeneous senescent cell populations. This review systematically discusses senescence-targeted engineered chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T immunotherapy, which achieves targeted clearance of pathological senescent cells by recognising specific surface markers. It summarises target-antigen evaluation frameworks, analyzes aged immunosuppressive microenvironment barriers and corresponding engineering strategies, and outlines composite efficacy assessment systems and tiered biomarker-monitoring workflows. Key translational bottlenecks such as imperfect antigen specificity and immune escape are also addressed. Preclinical studies verify organ function restoration and healthspan extension, while clinical evidence remains limited. Future integration of CAR-T technology with smart nanocarriers, synthetic biology and artificial intelligence will promote its clinical translation for senescence-associated disorders.

papers.abstract: The intratumoral microbiota plays a crucial role in cancer pathogenesis; however, the specific members involved and their mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify Bifidobacterium dentium (B. dentium ) as a tumor-associated bacterium enriched in fecal samples from patients with melanoma and colorectal cancer (CRC) and detectable in human melanoma and CRC tissues. High intratumoral B. dentium abundance correlates with poorer survival in CRC patients. In mouse models, subgingival administration of live B. dentium enables tumor homing and accelerated CT26 and B16F10 tumor growth, including in an orthotopic CT26 colorectal tumor model. Mechanistically, B. dentium invades tumor cells, promotes proliferation through Akt/ERK activation, enhances metastatic potential through MMP3 induction, and increases resistance to key chemotherapeutic agents. B. dentium-derived GABA activates FOXA2-dependent P-gp upregulation, contributing to chemotherapy resistance. These findings establish B. dentium as a niche-dependent pro-tumoral pathobiont and a potential target for improving cancer treatment response.

papers.abstract: Existing treatment options for colorectal and pancreatic cancers harboring mutant p53 (p53mut) are largely ineffective and lack selectivity. Our novel therapeutic strategy for p53mut cancers with a thymidine analogue (TAS102) and a PARP inhibitor (PARPi) showed promising efficacy in a clinical trial, although the mechanisms remain not fully understood. Here, we investigated the molecular mechanisms underlying therapeutic efficacy of our approach and explored new combinations to further enhance the response. To define the contribution of each drug into the therapeutic response, we conducted an unbiased transcriptomic analysis in p53-proficient and p53mut cancer models. The biological effects were investigated in comprehensive analyses of cell proliferation, cell death, and DNA damage. The drug interactions were explored in cytotoxicity assays and efficacy was tested in patient-derived colorectal and pancreatic cancer models. We found that TAS102-PARPi treatment induces DNA breaks and long G2-arrest in p53mut cells, whereas normal cells rapidly repair their DNA and re-enter the cell cycle. Transcriptomic analysis showed that TAS102 is the major driver of the response, whereas PARPi improves selectivity of the TAS102 effects. The treatment does not block replication in p53mut cells but induces post-replicative DNA repair and represses mitosis. Delayed blockade of G2-checkpoint results in massive cell death in p53mut cells selectively. Priming TAS102-PARPi treatment in combination with delayed G2-checkpoint blockade was highly effective against cancer models and was well-tolerated in mice. Broadly, a novel two-step therapeutic strategy showed high efficacy and selectivity for p53mut cancers and low toxicity to normal tissues, demonstrating potential for clinical translation.

papers.abstract: Summary Introduction Difficult tracheal intubation is associated with serious complications, including hypoxia, bradycardia and cardiac arrest. Neonates have increased physiologic vulnerability compared with older children, yet detailed data on management strategies and outcomes in neonates with difficult tracheal intubation remain limited. We hypothesised that clinicians have lower first‐attempt tracheal intubation success and higher complication rates for neonates compared with older children with difficult tracheal intubation. Methods We analysed the Pediatric Difficult Intubation Registry to determine tracheal intubation first attempt success and incidence of complications. We used logistic regression to identify variables associated with complications in neonates. Results During the study period, 6283 paediatric difficult tracheal intubations were recorded, including 420 neonates. First attempt success was lower for neonates (139/420, 33.1%) than older children (2394/4683, 51.1%). Complications occurred more frequently in neonates (123/420, 29.3%) than older children (637/4683, 13.6%). Hypoxia occurred in 92/420 (21.9%) neonates and 269/4683 (5.7%) older children. Severe complications were more frequent in neonates vs. older children (12/420, 2.9% vs. 30/4683, 0.6%, respectively), with cardiac arrests occurring in 4/420 (1.0%) neonates and 11/4683 (0.2%) older children. Difficult mask ventilation occurred more frequently in neonates (60/420, 14.3%) than older children (353/4681, 7.5%). In neonates, increased number of tracheal intubation attempts (aOR 1.61 per attempt, 95%CI 1.30–2.00, p < 0.001) and difficult facemask ventilation (aOR 3.17, 95%CI 1.38–7.30, p = 0.007) were associated with complications. Anticipated difficulty with airway management had a protective effect (aOR 0.37, 95%CI 0.16–0.88, p = 0.025). Discussion Neonates with difficult tracheal intubation experience a substantially higher rate of complications than older children. Early recognition of risk is critical in order to enable careful planning to minimise tracheal intubation attempts in this vulnerable population.

papers.abstract: This phase III, randomized, double-blind study (daNIS-2) evaluated the efficacy and safety of NIS793, an anti-transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) monoclonal antibody, in combination with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel [standard of care (SOC)] versus placebo and SOC as first-line treatment in patients with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (mPDAC). The study included a safety run-in (n = 21 patients enrolled) followed by a randomized part (n = 490 patients randomly assigned). Patients were assigned 1 : 1 to receive NIS793 or placebo with SOC. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS), secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), overall response rate (ORR), safety, pharmacokinetics, and exploratory biomarker analyses. The study was terminated early following an interim analysis due to an unfavorable benefit-risk profile. Median OS was 9.2 months in the NIS793 arm versus 11.2 months in the placebo arm (hazard ratio 1.26, 95% confidence interval 1.01-1.59). The estimates of ORR and median PFS indicate a less favorable treatment effect with NIS793. Safety profiles were comparable between arms, although higher rates of anemia, epistaxis, and rash were observed with NIS793; serious adverse events were more frequent in the NIS793 arm, with most being grade ≥3. Pharmacodynamic markers such as Pro-C3 supported target engagement. However, such target engagement did not translate into clinical benefit and early circulating tumor DNA dynamics were associated with less favorable outcomes. Biomarker analyses suggested that unfavorable benefit-risk profile of NIS793 was most pronounced in patients with a low epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition signature and a classical molecular subtype. NIS793 in combination with SOC did not improve survival outcomes in first-line mPDAC and was associated with an unfavorable benefit-risk profile. Exploratory biomarker findings highlight the complexity of TGF-β signaling and underscore the need for refined patient selection strategies in future trials.

papers.abstract: Heart rate (HR) and arterial blood pressure (BP) monitoring is standard of care during paediatric anaesthesia, yet evidence-based reference values for anaesthetised children remain limited. Existing BP reference values do not account for the combined effects of age, sex, weight, and height, and HR reference values in this population are lacking. We conducted a retrospective multicentre study using data from the Multicenter Perioperative Outcomes Group anaesthesia registry (2016-22). Included patients were aged <18 yr, ASA physical status 1 or 2, and undergoing noncardiac procedures under general anaesthesia. We used quantile regression to model the 2.3rd, 16th, 50th, 84th, and 97.7th centiles for HR, mean arterial pressure (MAP), systolic BP, and diastolic BP at two time points: the preparation phase (end of induction) and surgical phase (15-35 min after procedure start). Model covariates included age, sex, weight, and height. We selected the best model for each outcome using cross-validation with pinball loss. A total of 284 385 patients from 57 institutions were analysed. Optimal model complexity varied by outcome: a two-way interaction model was selected as the best-performing model for preparation phase HR and surgical phase MAP. A three-way interaction model was selected as the best-performing model for the remaining outcomes. Comprehensive prediction tables and an interactive web-based tool were developed for all outcomes. This study provides integrated HR and BP reference values for healthy paediatric patients undergoing general anaesthesia, incorporating age, sex, weight, and height simultaneously. These reference values with an interactive website can support clinical decision-making and haemodynamic monitoring.

papers.abstract: Recent clinical trials show prominent anti-tumor activity of CD73-blocking antibodies in combination with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) antagonists in a subset of patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), which highlights the need to understand the properties of the CD39/CD73 pathway in human lung malignancies and its modulation by other anti-cancer therapies. To address this, we study the distribution, biological context, spatial heterogeneity, clinical significance, and modulation of CD39/CD73 using multiplexed quantitative immunofluorescence and spatial transcriptomics analysis of multiple NSCLC patient cohorts, as well as in vitro experiments of cultured NSCLC cells. Our results reveal an asymmetric distribution of the CD39/CD73 pathway within the tumor microenvironment, preferential expression in lung adenocarcinomas with elevated PD-L1 and effector T cell infiltration or lacking STK11/KEAP1 mutations, limited intratumor spatial heterogeneity, and differential modulation of cancer cell CD73 by proinflammatory cytokines and systemic radio-chemotherapy. Collectively, our results can inform optimal design of therapeutic interventions and patient selection strategies.

papers.abstract: Summary Introduction Videolaryngoscopy has been associated with improved glottic visualisation and higher first‐attempt tracheal intubation success compared with direct laryngoscopy. However, multicentre evidence evaluating its effectiveness when tracheal intubation is performed by anaesthesia resident doctors in routine practice is limited. Methods Adult patients undergoing surgery requiring tracheal intubation were assigned to videolaryngoscopy or direct laryngoscopy for the initial attempt. All tracheal intubations were performed by anaesthesia residents under consultant supervision. The primary outcome was successful tracheal intubation on the first attempt. Secondary outcomes included glottic visualisation; number of tracheal intubation attempts; need for adjunct airway devices; procedural difficulty; and procedural complications. Results We enrolled 1001 patients and assigned 501 to videolaryngoscopy and 500 patients to direct laryngoscopy. Successful first‐attempt tracheal intubation was achieved in 397 (79.2%) patients allocated to the videolaryngoscopy group and 351 (70.2%) patients allocated to the direct laryngoscopy group (absolute risk difference 9.0%, 95%CI 3.7–14.4%, p < 0.001). Videolaryngoscopy improved glottic visualisation, with more patients having a modified Cormack–Lehane grade 2 or 2a view (467/501 (93.3%) vs. 404/500 (80.8%); p < 0.001); decreased operator‐reported tracheal intubation difficulty (168/501 (33.5%) vs. 236/500 (47.2%); p < 0.001) and reduced procedural complications (39/501 (7.7%) vs. 91/500 (18.2%); p < 0.001), without a clinically meaningful difference in tracheal intubation time or the need for adjunct airway devices. Discussion In adult patients undergoing tracheal intubation by anaesthesia resident doctors, videolaryngoscopy increased first‐attempt success and improved overall procedural performance compared with direct laryngoscopy.

papers.abstract: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) remains incurable and autologous T-cell-based therapies induce durable remissions in only a minority of patients. Although poor T-cell performance in CLL has been attributed to exhaustion, T cells from CLL patients retain cytokine production and lack key transcriptional markers of exhaustion, suggesting an alternative state of differentiation. Here, we performed an integrated phenotypic, epigenetic and functional analysis of circulating CD8⁺ T cells from treatment-naive CLL patients to define the nature and therapeutic relevance of terminal differentiation in CLL. CD8⁺ T cells from treatment-naive CLL patients were enriched for a terminally differentiated, CD27⁻CD28⁻CD57⁺KLRG1⁺ population with several senescence-associated features, including increased cell size, granularity, β-galactosidase activity, and reduced basal autophagy. However, these cells lacked key hallmarks of irreversible senescence. Instead, CLL T cells mounted robust but transient proliferative bursts and developed activation-associated γH2AX signals followed by impaired persistence and increased cell death upon repeated activation. Especially CD57⁺ T cells were vulnerable and incompatible with the experimental steps required for CAR T-cell manufacturing. The potent, acute effector function of these cells could, however, be harnessed by bispecific T-cell engagers, which induced effective cytolysis of both cell lines and primary CLL targets by these T cells. Collectively, our data support a model in which CD8+ T-cell dysfunction in CLL reflects accumulation of short-lived, terminally differentiated effector cells rather than canonical exhaustion or irreversible senescence. This state limits durable persistence required for CAR T-cell approached while preserving acute cytotoxicity relevant for bispecific antibody-based therapies in CLL.

papers.abstract: Immunoglobulin light chains (LCs) span the spectrum of B-cell clonal disorders from monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance to multiple myeloma and Waldenström macroglobulinemia. Beyond serving as disease markers, monoclonal immunoglobulins can cause organ damage in monoclonal gammopathies of clinical significance (MGCS). In AL amyloidosis the pathogenic agent is a monoclonal light chain (LC). AL amyloidosis is a treatable yet rapidly progressive condition in which early diagnosis is critical for organ preservation and survival. High-sensitivity laboratory tools for detection of amyloidogenic LCs are essential in diagnosis, while precise quantitative methods are required for monitoring treatment response and for identifying relapse, where standardized relapse definitions remain an unmet need. With increasingly effective therapies, deep hematologic response assessment and measurable residual disease detection-through mass spectrometry-based methods, flow cytometry, and next-generation sequencing-are central to decision-making. Emerging strategies to discriminate "innocent" from amyloidogenic LCs will enable pre-symptomatic intervention in patients with apparently benign monoclonal gammopathies. These approaches include biomarkers of early organ damage and LC-intrinsic features that enhance amyloid propensity (N-glycosylation, preferential germline gene usage, and reduced stability). Such tools also hold promise for the differential diagnosis of non-AL amyloidoses, particularly transthyretin (ATTR) cardiac amyloidosis-the most common form in elderly males and African-American populations-who are at elevated risk of coexisting LC-producing clones. Rapid and accurate exclusion of AL amyloidosis in this setting is now a clinical imperative. This review synthesizes current laboratory approaches and future directions for LC detection and monitoring in systemic amyloidoses, highlighting their impact on hematologic practice.

papers.abstract: To estimate the relative and absolute risks (ARs) for ovarian, prostate, male and female breast, pancreatic, biliary tract, and colorectal cancers associated with germline BARD1 pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants (PVs/LPVs) because these risks have not previously been reported from a genotype-first perspective. We performed a secondary retrospective analysis of multicenter data comprising 445 three-generation pedigrees with confirmed BARD1 PVs/LPVs from 25 institutions nationwide. Data were aggregated at the family-relatedness level. The risks were estimated using a Bayesian survival model that incorporated information from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program. We confirmed the previously established increased risk for female breast cancer (relative risk [RR] = 3.53; 95% CI, 1.95 to 5.81; posterior probability [PP] = 0.0040) and found positive associations with female pancreatic cancer (RR = 3.76 [95% CI, 2.16-7.25]; PP < .0001), male pancreatic cancer (RR = 2.89 [95% CI, 1.66 to 5.61]; PP < .0001), and prostate cancer (RR = 3.02 [95% CI, 1.95 to 4.71]; PP < .0001). The predictive ARs to age 85 were 41.84% (95% CI, 23.09 to 68.91) for female breast cancer, 4.80% (95% CI, 2.76 to 9.25) for female pancreatic cancer, 3.98% (95% CI, 2.29 to 7.73) for male pancreatic cancer, and 36.11% (95% CI, 23.29 to 56.29) for prostate cancer. Risk estimates suggest an association for male breast, ovarian, and female colorectal cancers; however, the clinical significance is unclear, and these findings warrant cautious interpretation. In contrast, we found no evidence of association for biliary tract cancer or male colorectal cancer. These results support BARD1's association with female breast cancer and suggest associations with pancreatic and prostate cancers. These findings have potential implications for genetic counseling and personalized risk management for male and female BARD1 PV/LPV heterozygotes.

papers.abstract: Lymph node metastasis (LNM) represents a pivotal event in cancer progression and a major determinant of response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). Elucidation of the molecular mechanisms linking metastatic dissemination to immune suppression could identify potential therapeutic targets to improve ICB efficacy. Here, we identified the coagulation initiator tissue factor (F3) as a central regulator bridging tumor metastasis and immune evasion in gastric cancer (GC). F3 was significantly upregulated in LNM-positive tumors and correlated with impaired ICB responsiveness and poor clinical outcome. Mechanistically, the intracellular domain of F3 directly bound eEF1A1 to promote STAT3 phosphorylation and induce CCL20 expression, which selectively recruited CCR6+ regulatory T cells (Tregs) to establish an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Disruption of this F3-eEF1A1-STAT3-CCL20 axis with the clinically approved compound olsalazine disodium served as a compelling preclinical proof-of-concept to potently suppress tumor growth, abrogate Treg infiltration, and restore ICB sensitivity, all without perturbing basal coagulation. These findings redefine F3 from a canonical coagulation initiator to a tumor-intrinsic immunomodulator and reveal a druggable vulnerability that uncouples its oncogenic signaling from hemostasis.

papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) are heterogeneous myeloid malignancies with limited therapeutic options and often poor long-term prognosis due to persistence of therapy-resistant leukemic stem cells (LSC). Immunotherapeutic approaches have demonstrated high efficacy in lymphoid malignancies, but their application in AML and CMML remains challenging due to the lack of targetable (neo-)antigens. Here we investigated the expression of the adhesion G protein-coupled receptor E2 (ADGRE2) in diagnostic samples from 124 AML and 28 CMML patients using multiparameter flow cytometry and publicly available expression databases. ADGRE2 was significantly overexpressed on leukemic blasts in both AML and CMML compared to normal CD34+ hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). ADGRE2 surface expression was high within the CD34+/38- and GPR56high LSC-enriched compartments, comparably distributed with minor differences among subgroups and high in distinct samples with low expression of established immunotherapeutic targets, such as CD33 and CLL-1. Our findings further corroborate ADGRE2 as a promising (complementary) immunotherapeutic target in myeloid malignancies.

papers.abstract: Histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) is a key biological macromolecule involved in protein acetylation and inflammatory signalling. Although its biological functions are well recognised, the molecular mechanisms through which HDAC3 regulates stress-induced responses of alveolar epithelial cells during early-stage radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) remain incompletely understood. In this study, using AT2-specific HDAC3 conditional knockout mice as well as primary mouse AT2 and A549 cell models, we found that radiation markedly upregulates HDAC3 expression, whereas HDAC3 knockdown alleviates radiation-induced disruption of the alveolar epithelial barrier. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed that HDAC3 influences barrier integrity by modulating MAPK-mediated inflammation and apoptosis. Pharmacological intervention with the selective HDAC3 inhibitor RGFP966 also demonstrated that HDAC3 inhibition mitigates radiation-induced oxidative stress imbalance. Mechanistically, HDAC3 deacetylates MKP1, enhancing p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK) phosphorylation, promoting FBJ murine osteosarcoma viral oncogene homolog (c-Fos) expression, and activating activator protein-1 (AP-1), thereby driving downstream inflammatory signalling. Collectively, our findings support a role for the HDAC3-MKP1-p38 MAPK-c-Fos/AP-1 axis in regulating inflammatory responses in AT2 cells and highlight HDAC3 as a potential molecular target for mitigating alveolar epithelial injury in early-stage RILI.

papers.abstract: Nonmelanoma skin cancer (NMSC) is one of the most common malignancies worldwide, with increasing incidence. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a prevalent comorbidity that may adversely affect cancer prognosis through shared metabolic and inflammatory pathways. This study aims to identify risk factors influencing the survival of NMSC patients with T2DM, construct and evaluate the performance of different predictive models, and develop a comprehensive risk score to accurately predict the survival probability of these patients. We collected data from the Hong Kong Hospital Authority Data Collaboration Laboratory, including 1325 NMSC patients with T2DM between 2000 and 2020. Cox proportional hazards (CoxPH), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator-Cox model (LASSO-Cox), random survival forest (RSF), and survival tree were employed to construct prediction models. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was conducted to identify key risk factors and attribute model outputs. A risk score system was developed using the AutoScore-Survival package. We identified seven significant predictors for poorer overall survival among patients with T2DM, including higher age at cancer diagnosis, male sex, smoking, longer duration of T2DM, elevated creatinine and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and lower fasting glucose. The RSF model showed the highest predictive performance among the evaluated machine learning models. The tuned AutoScore-Survival risk score system demonstrated good predictive performance (concordance index (C-index) = 0.712 in the test set), and was based on the following variables: age at cancer diagnosis, duration of T2DM, creatinine, insulin treatment, stroke, and HbA1c. The areas under the curve (AUCs) at 1, 3, and 5 years in the test set were 0.677, 0.697, and 0.729, respectively. Older age at cancer diagnosis, male sex, longer diabetes duration, smoking, elevated creatinine and HbA1c, and lower fasting glucose were identified as adverse prognostic factors for NMSC patients with T2DM. The RSF model outperformed other algorithms in predictive accuracy. The proposed risk score offers a clinically interpretable and effective means of predicting survival among NMSC patients with T2DM.

papers.abstract: Tissue stiffening is a predominant malignant physical alteration in cancer progression, yet its effect on specific immune subsets within the tumor microenvironment is not well defined. Here we show that elevated tissue stiffness subverts tumor-infiltrating type 1 helper T (TH1) cells to drive immunosuppression in pancreatic cancer. Mechanistically, stiffness triggers integrin-mediated mechanotransduction to activate YAP, which translocates to the nucleus and cooperates with RUNX1 to transcriptionally upregulate a set of dysfunction-associated genes. These reprogrammed TH1 cells acquire a distinct dysfunction-associated secretory phenotype, which in turn drives M2-like polarization of macrophages and amplifies local immunosuppression. Notably, inhibiting YAP expression or disrupting YAP-RUNX1 interaction reverses the dysfunctional state of TH1 cells and restores antitumor immunity. These findings delineate a mechano-immunological mechanism by which tumor stiffness subverts TH1 cell functions, indicating a possible therapeutic avenue to alleviate immunosuppression and potentiate immunotherapy efficacy in stiff tumors.

papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus-positive gastric cancer (EBV(+) GC) shows extensive DNA hypermethylation in gene promoter regions. DNA methylation induced by EBV infection contributes to carcinogenesis through tumor suppressor gene inactivation. Whereas aberrant DNA methylation in enhancer regions might reportedly contribute to carcinogenesis, its impact has not been fully elucidated. Therefore, we here performed DNA methylome analysis on clinical samples, including GC and normal gastric mucosa, using the Infinium MethylationEPIC BeadChip array to evaluate the epigenome in the enhancer regions. We stratified GC cases into three subclusters using hierarchical clustering analysis based on the methylation status of enhancer regions; EBV(+) GC samples were classified into the most extensively methylated subcluster. We identified genes with promoters unmethylated but enhancers aberrantly methylated in EBV(+) GC. Such methylated genes included Inositol polyphosphate-5-phosphatase A (INPP5A), which is associated with the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/Akt signaling pathway and cell proliferation and survival, and showed lower expression levels in EBV(+) GC compared with normal mucosa and other GC samples. We infected GES1, an immortalized gastric epithelial cell line, with EBV in vitro, and demonstrated the induction of aberrant DNA methylation in the INPP5A enhancer region and the downregulation of its expression. These findings indicate that EBV(+) GC exhibits a specific DNA hypermethylation phenotype in enhancer regions, and EBV infection in gastric cells could induce aberrant DNA methylation in enhancer regions, involving dysregulation of cancer-related gene expression.

papers.abstract: This study investigated the expression, prognostic significance, and functional role of α-L-iduronidase (IDUA) in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). We performed two-sample Mendelian randomization using eQTL and ccRCC GWAS data. We analyzed transcriptomic and clinical data from TCGA and GEO cohorts. We constructed a prognostic nomogram integrating IDUA expression with clinicopathological variables. We used ESTIMATE and CIBERSORT algorithms to evaluate immune infiltration and examined correlations between IDUA and immune checkpoint genes. We knocked down IDUA in 786-O and ACHN cells using shRNA and assessed proliferation, invasion, and migration via MTT, Transwell, and wound-healing assays. IDUA was significantly overexpressed in ccRCC tumors versus normal tissues. High IDUA expression correlated with advanced stage, higher T stage, and poor overall survival. Multivariate Cox regression confirmed IDUA as an independent prognostic factor (HR = 1.614, p < 0.001). The nomogram showed good predictive performance for 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival. IDUA expression positively correlated with immune checkpoint genes (PDCD1, CD274, CTLA4) and with infiltration of CD8+ T cells, Tregs, and activated NK cells. High IDUA predicted higher Immunophenoscores, suggesting better immunotherapy response. In vitro, IDUA knockdown significantly reduced ccRCC cell proliferation, invasion, and migration. IDUA serves as an independent prognostic biomarker in ccRCC, promotes tumor aggressiveness, and may modulate the immune microenvironment. These findings support IDUA as a potential therapeutic target and a candidate predictor for immunotherapy response in ccRCC.

papers.abstract: Lymph node (LN) metastasis is a major determinant of clinical outcome in gastric cancer (GC), yet the molecular and spatial features of metastatic LN niches remain incompletely defined. Here, we integrated digital spatial profiling (DSP) of primary GC and matched LNs, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and 10x Genomics Visium spatial transcriptomics. Cross-sectional analysis of cytokeratin-positive regions across primary GC and N1-N3 metastatic lymph nodes (mLNs) identified a hybrid epithelial-mesenchymal expression pattern in N1 samples and prominent immune checkpoint, angiogenic, and receptor tyrosine kinase programs in the N3 group. Deconvolution showed enrichment of exhausted T cells, regulatory T cells, and fibroblasts in mLNs, consistent with immunosuppressive remodeling of the local microenvironment. Cell-cell communication analysis implicated the galectin-9 (LGALS9)-CD45/CD44, CLEC2D-KLRB1, and CCL19/CCL21-CCR7 axes in mLNs. Spatial analysis further revealed compartment-specific heterogeneity, including distinct proliferative, immune, and immunosuppressive programs. Integrating multiple transcriptomic datasets, we derived a 12-gene lymph node metastasis gene signature (LNMGS); high LNMGS scores were associated with poorer overall survival in the TCGA-STAD cohort. Spatial mapping of the LNMGS in primary GC identified an LNMGS-high region displaying a center-to-periphery expression gradient and tending to have a higher inferred copy-number burden. A distance-associated gene signature derived from this gradient was enriched for proliferation, invasion, angiogenesis, immune evasion, and stemness. Together, these findings provide a spatial and molecular framework for lymph node metastasis in GC and highlight potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for further investigation. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

papers.abstract: Pre-operative stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) and intraoperative cesium-131 (Cs-131) brachytherapy are alternatives to post-operative SRS for resected brain metastases (BMs). The randomized phase 3 Radiation One and Done Study (ROADS; NCT04365374) showed improved surgical-bed control with Cs-131 tiles versus post-operative stereotactic radiotherapy, but outcomes relative to pre-operative SRS are undefined. PubMed, Embase, and ScienceDirect were searched through October 2026 (PRISMA 2020); one further trial was identified by other methods. Twelve-month local control (LC), leptomeningeal disease (LMD), radiation necrosis (RN), and overall survival (OS) were extracted for treatment-naïve BMs. Proportions were pooled with random-effects generalized linear mixed models and compared with a test for subgroup differences; sensitivity analyses included meta-regression, Hartung-Knapp, leave-one-out, follow-up, and fractionation analyses. Fifteen pre-operative SRS studies (918 patients/940 BMs) and four brachytherapy studies (207 patients/217 BMs) were included. Pooled 12-month LC was 97% (95% CI 90-99) with Cs-131 brachytherapy and 90% (86-93) with pre-operative SRS (test for subgroup differences p = 0.054; meta-regression p = 0.019; Hartung-Knapp p = 0.066); among studies reporting observed counts, LC was 99% vs. 90% (p = 0.009). Within pre-operative SRS, LC was 96% after hypofractionated and 86% after single-fraction treatment (p = 0.005). LMD (9.1% vs. 5.1%) and RN (0.7% vs. 5.2%) did not differ significantly. Median OS was 15.6 months with brachytherapy (range 5.9-42.5; 11.0 months, range 5.9-20.1, excluding the ROADS estimate) and 14.4 months with pre-operative SRS (range 6.3-26.4). Both approaches achieved high LC with low rates of LMD and RN. There was a trend towards higher LC with Cs-131 brachytherapy than with pre-operative SRS (97% vs. 90%; p = 0.054), and significantly so among studies reporting observed counts (99% vs. 90%; p = 0.009). Hypofractionated pre-operative SRS achieved LC similar to that of brachytherapy, suggesting that the difference may reflect single-fraction dose de-escalation rather than an intrinsic advantage of either modality. The two techniques may serve complementary roles, and prospective comparative study is warranted. This review was not registered in PROSPERO.

papers.abstract: Impaired pulmonary epithelial cell homeostasis is a key pathogenic feature in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Mucin 1 (MUC1/Muc1) is a membrane-tethered glycoprotein that plays important roles in modulating various disease progression. This study aims to decipher the role and mechanisms of MUC1 in the pathogenesis of COPD. We found functional variants (rs4072037 T > C and rs12411216 C > A) in MUC1 were associated with increased susceptibility to COPD. MUC1-C expression in lung tissues was age-dependent, elevated in adults but decreased in elderly COPD patients. Aged Muc1-deficient mice showed increased cellular senescence in alveolar type II (AT2) epithelial cells and spontaneously developed emphysema. In cigarette smoke (CS)-induced COPD model mice, Muc1 deficiency caused an accelerated decline in lung function, impaired mitochondrial function, enhanced lung inflammation, and impaired AT2-to- alveolar type I (AT1) epithelial cell transdifferentiation. Adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9)-mediated AT2 cell-specific reconstitution of Muc1 ameliorated COPD in association with integrated suppression of pulmonary inflammation and enhancement of AT2 transdifferentiation and mitochondrial function. Mechanistically, we found MUC1 attenuated senescence and associated cell dysfunction, including activation of PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy flux and AMPK/NDUFS4-driven mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming in AT2 cells. In addition, MUC1 modulated CS extract (CSE)-induced human AT2-to-AT1 transdifferentiation through enhancement of β-catenin nuclear translocation. Moreover, overexpression of MUC1 in lung epithelial cells inhibited CS-induced NF-κB activation and inflammatory responses in both in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, this study identified MUC1 as a protective molecule and potential target for COPD, particularly emphysema, via facilitating AT2-to-AT1 cell transdifferentiation, while prohibiting senescence and inflammation.

papers.abstract: Chronic diseases exhibit multiscale heterogeneity and spatial organization, yet analytical frameworks often fail to connect molecular perturbations, tissue architecture, and clinical outcomes within a unified evidence framework. Bulk and single-modality approaches can identify regulatory or cellular alterations but provide limited insight into why pathogenic programs emerge in anatomical regions, how they shape disease niches, and how they drive divergent clinical trajectories. Multi-omics partially addresses this gap by resolving interconnected layers of regulation, transcription, protein activity, and metabolism, whereas spatial omics maps these processes within preserved tissue architecture, enabling the delineation of lesion topology, interface states, and multicellular microenvironments. Artificial intelligence (AI) may further extend this framework by integrating molecular, spatial, imaging, and clinical data into disease representations that support disease stratification, the discovery of mechanistic patterns, and clinically testable predictions, provided that models are externally validated, biologically interpretable, and robust to dataset bias and domain shift. In this review, we examine how multi-omics, spatial omics, and AI can bridge the disconnect between molecular profiling, spatial pathology, and clinical translation in chronic disease research. We discuss six representative disease domains before synthesizing insights into how these approaches define molecular endotypes, map pathological niches, identify recurrent mechanistic patterns, and generate interpretable surrogate readouts for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment stratification. We also highlight limitations, including preanalytical variability, inconsistencies across platforms, limited external generalizability, and the challenges of translating high-dimensional outputs into deployable clinical tools. Finally, we outline priorities for scalable evidence systems, mechanism-guided validation frameworks, multimodal model interpretability, and prospective clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Intraoperative hypotension is a common complication in pediatric anesthesia. The definition of hypotension and treatment strategies are heterogeneous. The association of these treatments with cerebral regional oxygen saturation, measured by near‐infrared spectroscopy, is insufficiently characterized. Aims The study explores whether changes in cerebral regional oxygen saturation, mean arterial pressure, and heart rate differ after the administration of an isotonic fluid bolus, noradrenaline, adrenaline, or cafedrine/theodrenaline for perioperative hypotension in children. Methods This single‐center, observational pilot study included children aged 18 years or younger undergoing noncardiac surgery who developed hypotension requiring treatment. The choice of the intervention was at the discretion of the attending anesthetist and guided by an internal guideline. Cerebral regional oxygen saturation, mean arterial pressure, and heart rate were recorded for 8 min after the first intervention and analyzed relative to the value immediately before treatment. Groups were compared using the area under the curve of these changes and linear mixed‐effects models. Results Forty‐six patients were analyzed. Cerebral regional oxygen saturation immediately before treatment did not differ from the pre‐induction baseline. Cafedrine/theodrenaline was the only treatment associated with a sustained increase in cerebral regional oxygen saturation, with a significantly higher area under the curve than noradrenaline ( p = 0.017), adrenaline ( p = 0.017), and fluid administration ( p < 0.001), which was confirmed by mixed‐effects models. Only cafedrine/theodrenaline was associated with an increase in heart rate. Changes in heart rate were significantly correlated with changes in cerebral regional oxygen saturation (Spearman's ρ = 0.376, p = 0.010), but not with changes in mean arterial pressure. Conclusions Cafedrine/theodrenaline was associated with a sustained increase in cerebral regional oxygen saturation, heart rate, and blood pressure. Noradrenaline, adrenaline, and fluid administration were associated with unchanged or decreasing cerebral regional oxygen saturation. Randomized controlled studies are required to confirm these findings.

papers.abstract: Real-world analyses of biomarker-matched therapy (BMT) are complicated when sequencing, surgery, and treatment occur at different times. We evaluated associations between BMT and overall survival (OS) by surgical status at sequencing and specimen source and examined treatment timing. Among 6624 patients with non-small cell lung cancer in MSK-CHORD, 5467 with an operational opportunity for BMT formed the propensity-weighted cohort. OS was measured from first sequencing; surgical status reflected surgery completed by that date. Fixed-exposure analyses used stabilized inverse probability of treatment weights. The overall HR was 1.10 (95% CI 1.01-1.20). HRs were 1.40 (1.23-1.59) with surgery completed by sequencing and 0.83 (0.74-0.93) without surgery, and 1.30 (1.15-1.47) for primary-tumor specimens and 0.80 (0.71-0.91) for metastatic-site specimens; interaction tests were significant (all p < 0.001). Time-dependent HRs were 2.06 (1.76-2.42) and 1.12 (0.99-1.26) by surgical status, and 1.76 (1.52-2.03) and 1.14 (1.01-1.30) by specimen source. Landmark analyses did not retain the lower fixed-exposure estimates in the no-surgery and metastatic-specimen strata. In a 685-patient non-MSK metastatic cohort, HRs were 0.88 (0.63-1.25) for primary-tumor sequencing and 0.64 (0.48-0.84) for metastatic-site sequencing. BMT-OS associations were sensitive to clinical context and treatment timing, underscoring temporal alignment of sequencing, surgery, treatment initiation, and follow-up.

papers.abstract: Established risk factors account for a small proportion of lymphoid and myeloid neoplasms; many associations have not been conclusively established, etiologic differences across certain subtypes are poorly understood, and most studies have been conducted in Western populations. Investigations in populations with differing exposure patterns, subtype distributions, and genetic architecture are needed to fully understand hematopoietic tumor etiology. To this end, we conducted a large, multicenter, hospital-based case-control study of lymphoid and myeloid neoplasms in East Asia (AsiaLymph), including 5671 lymphoid cases, 1879 myeloid cases, and 3858 controls. Participants completed an interview and provided biospecimens. Cases underwent central pathology review and were coded into the World Health Organization classification. Herein, we describe the study methods and report associations for body mass index (BMI), education, and family history. Higher BMI at age 20 but not 40 was associated with lymphoid (per 5 kg/m2: OR [95% CI]: 1.18 [1.09-1.27]) and myeloid (1.17 [1.05-1.29]) neoplasms. Greater educational attainment was associated with lymphoid (for college versus < primary education: 1.41 [1.21-1.65]) but not myeloid (1.17 [0.95-1.45]; p-heterogeneity < 0.01) neoplasms. There were also positive associations between first-degree family history of hematologic cancer and lymphoid (1.53 [1.15-2.03]) and myeloid (1.65 [1.11-2.44]) neoplasms. In analyses of major subtypes, these risk factors were not associated with NK/T-cell lymphoma, suggesting a distinct etiology for this subtype. AsiaLymph is one of the largest molecular epidemiology studies of both lymphoid and myeloid neoplasms with central pathology review and will serve as a valuable resource for etiologic investigations into these malignancies.

papers.abstract: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist semaglutide improves symptoms in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) through unclear mechanisms. Here, in this double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, we randomly assigned 81 patients (47 women) with HFpEF and obesity to semaglutide (2.4 mg weekly) or placebo for 52 weeks. The primary outcome was the change in invasively measured pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP), a direct measure of cardiac congestion, during low-intensity exercise. Additional mechanistic outcomes included other hemodynamic measures and hemodynamic HFpEF remission (defined as normal PAWP under conditions of both rest and exercise at 52 weeks). At baseline, PAWP was 17.5 ± 4.3 mmHg at rest and 31.7 ± 5.2 mmHg during exercise. After 52 weeks, the mean change in PAWP during exercise was -9.8 (95% confidence interval (CI): -11.3 to -8.2) mmHg with semaglutide and +0.9 (95% CI: -1.3 to 3.0) mmHg with placebo (estimated difference, -10.6 mmHg; 95% CI: -13.3 to -8.0; P < 0.0001). As compared to placebo, semaglutide also decreased resting PAWP (estimated difference, -7.1 mmHg; 95% CI: -9.8 to -4.4; P < 0.0001), and semaglutide-treated patients were more likely to experience hemodynamic remission (53.7% versus 7.4%, odds ratio = 14.1, 95% CI: 3.0-134.6, P < 0.001). The results from this trial indicate that, in patients with HFpEF and obesity, treatment with semaglutide reduced left heart filling pressures during exercise and at rest and was associated with hemodynamic HFpEF remission in over half of treated patients. papers.abstract: This analysis of NRG/RTOG 0424 describes post-treatment changes in neurocognitive function (NCF) and quality of life (QOL) in patients with high-risk low-grade glioma (HR-LGG). Patients with HR-LGG were treated with radiation and concurrent and adjuvant temozolomide (RT-TMZ). Standardized NCF tests were performed at baseline, 6, and 12 months. Rates of change in NCF were examined using the reliable change index (RCI) on Hopkins Verbal Learning Test (HVLT), Trail Making Test (TMT), and Controlled Oral Word Association (COWA). Relationships between NCF and subjective cognitive concerns (MOS-CF) were evaluated. QOL was assessed using Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy - Brain (FACT-Br). Longitudinal modeling evaluated predictors of change in NCF and QOL. Cox models assessed the association of baseline NCF with overall survival (OS). From January 2005 to August 2009, 129 evaluable patients were accrued, and 93 completed at least the baseline and one post-treatment NCF/QOL measurement. RCI-determined decline occurred in 50% and 40% at 6 and 12 months, respectively and was most frequent on HVLT (21%, 20%), TMTA (29%, 20%), and TMTB (22%, 14%). MID-determined QOL decline on the FACT-Brain Subscale occurred in about 25% at 6 and 12 months. Several tumor and clinical characteristics were associated with worse NCF including tumor crossing the midline, the number of high-risk factors, and EORTC OS risk group. Many patients with HR-LGG experience NCF decline in the first year after treatment with temozolomide-based concurrent chemoradiation. QOL remained stable or improved. Ongoing studies with integrated NCF monitoring using these tests will aid clinicians and patients in treatment decisions that seek to consider oncologic and functional outcomes.

papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists improve symptoms in patients with obesity and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). We recently demonstrated that semaglutide reduces exertional pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) in obesity-related HFpEF, but potential effects of semaglutide on cardiac structure and function that may underlie these hemodynamic improvements remain unclear. In this prespecified cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) substudy of the randomized CAMEO-SEMA trial, 49 participants (33 semaglutide, 16 placebo, 28 female) underwent CMR at baseline and 52 weeks, within 1 day of invasive exercise hemodynamic assessment. The prespecified primary CMR endpoint was change in left atrial (LA) reservoir strain; other prespecified CMR endpoints included LV filling dynamics, which were assessed by early filling rate indexed to end-diastolic volume (eFR/EDV). Compared with placebo, semaglutide improved LA reservoir strain (+5.7% [95% CI, +0.3 to +9.7]; P=0.037) and eFR/EDV (+0.64 s-1 [95% CI, +0.42 to +1.00]; P<0.0001). Improvements in LA reservoir strain and LV filling dynamics were associated with reductions in exercise PAWP (r=-0.46, P<0.001 and r=-0.65, P<0.0001, respectively). With respect to other prespecified CMR endpoints, semaglutide reduced LV mass, restored more physiologic LV geometry, and improved right ventricular function and biventricular myocardial mechanics. The results of this CMR substudy indicate that in patients with obesity-related HFpEF, semaglutide improves LA function and LV diastolic filling dynamics, identifying improvements in myocardial function that may contribute to semaglutide's improvement of hemodynamics. papers.abstract: Abstract China’s oncology drug development ecosystem has shifted from rapid pipeline expansion toward clinical value–driven innovation. We review regulatory reform and the 2015 to 2025 evolution of clinical development across small molecules, mAbs, multispecific antibodies, antibody–drug conjugates, and cell and gene therapies. China’s disease burden and enrollment capacity have enabled globally relevant advances in EGFR-mutant lung cancer, gastrointestinal malignancies, hepatocellular carcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and CLDN18.2-directed therapies. We highlight persistent challenges in target and modality convergence, biomarker definition, therapeutic window optimization, manufacturing consistency, and globally interpretable evidence generation and discuss how artificial intelligence may connect target discovery, drug design, and clinical trial optimization more efficiently. Significance: China has become a major source of oncology trials and modality innovation, but scale alone will not ensure global impact. This review links regulatory reform, disease-specific opportunity, target biology, therapeutic format, and evidence quality across a decade of solid tumor development. It defines the conditions under which China-originated programs can generate globally practice-changing evidence. See related article by Shi, p. XX .

papers.abstract: Local therapy has recently been applied to treat oligometastatic cancer across various malignant cancers. However, definitive evidence for local treatment regimens remains lacking. We aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of combining local therapy with systemic treatment for patients with oligometastatic solid tumors including breast cancer, liver cancer, and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a multicenter retrospective study. From January 2013 to December 2023, 575 patients with fewer than or equal to five metastases of breast cancer, liver cancer, and NSCLC in three tertiary university hospitals were analyzed retrospectively. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS). The secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS) and prognostic factors affecting the treatment outcomes. Before propensity score matching, significant differences were observed in both OS and PFS between the local therapy plus systemic therapy and systemic therapy alone groups (p < 0.001 and p < 0.001). After PSM, PFS remained significantly different (p = 0.017), but OS did not (p = 0.076). In liver cancer, before PSM analysis showed a significant PFS benefit (p = 0.011), which was absent after PSM for both OS and PFS (p = 0.568 and p = 0.363). For both breast cancer and NSCLC patients, no significant differences in OS or PFS were found after PSM. Local treatment of solitary metastatic lesions showed that no statistically significant difference was observed in OS or PFS of patients with advanced oligometastatic breast, liver cancer, and NSCLC.

papers.abstract: High-temperature requirement protease A3 (HtrA3) has been implicated in the progression of various carcinomas through tissue-specific mechanisms; however, its precise role in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains unclear. We initially identified the upregulation of HtrA3 in CRC tissues through Isobaric Tags for Relative and Absolute Quantitation (iTRAQ) proteomics, which was consistent with the analysis of the CPTAC dataset. Our research further confirmed that HtrA3 is significantly upregulated in CRC tissues and associated with reduced overall survival. Functional assays showed that HtrA3 overexpression enhanced CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while HtrA3 knockdown yielded opposite effects. In HtrA3-overexpressing HCT116 cells, increased phosphorylation of PI3K, AKT, and FOXO1 was observed, which was reduced upon treatment with the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. Conversely, in HtrA3-knockdown SW480 cells, these phosphorylation levels declined but were restored with the PI3K activator 740Y-P. In vivo, HtrA3 overexpression accelerated xenograft tumor growth. These findings suggest that HtrA3 promotes CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, potentially involving PI3K-AKT-FOXO1 signaling, and support further investigation of HtrA3 as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in CRC.

papers.abstract: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) is a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) with a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload and was approved by the Japan Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency in 2025 for patients with unresectable or recurrent hormone receptor-positive (HR+)/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) breast cancer previously treated with chemotherapy. In the pivotal TROPION-Breast01 trial, most patients had received 1 or 2 prior systemic regimens. However, in routine clinical practice, Dato-DXd is often used in heavily pretreated patients, including those with prior ADC exposure. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of Dato-DXd in this population. We retrospectively analyzed 18 patients with HR+/HER2- metastatic or recurrent breast cancer who received Dato-DXd at our institution between May and December 2025. Clinical data from electronic medical records were reviewed to assess treatment efficacy and treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). All patients were female, with a median age of 56 years (range, 48-81). Patients were heavily pretreated, with a median of seven prior systemic treatment lines (range, 2-11); 72.2% had previously received trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd). Median real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS) was 3.2 months. Patients with prior T-DXd exposure had significantly shorter rwPFS than T-DXd-naïve patients (2.8 vs. 6.4 months, p < 0.01). TRAEs were generally mild and manageable. The most common TRAEs included alopecia, fatigue, constipation, stomatitis, nausea, and elevated liver transaminases. Five patients required dose reductions, but no treatment discontinuations or fatal events occurred. No cases of interstitial lung disease occurred. In this cohort of heavily pretreated HR+/HER2- metastatic or recurrent breast cancer, Dato-DXd showed limited clinical activity compared with clinical trials, particularly among patients previously treated with T-DXd. Nevertheless, Dato-DXd was safely administered with toxicity management. Further real-world studies are needed to optimize patient selection and treatment sequencing.

papers.abstract: Patients with clinically node-positive (cN1) breast cancer represent a heterogeneous population with evolving axillary management strategies. We evaluated whether extent of axillary nodal involvement is associated with survival in cN1 disease. A retrospective study of patients with cT1-4N1M0 breast cancer and biopsy-proven axillary metastasis (2012-2018) was performed. All patients underwent axillary ultrasound (AUS) prior to neoadjuvant systemic therapy (NST) and again before surgery. Kaplan-Meier method and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used for statistical analysis. Among 825 patients, most had cT2-3 (75.6%), hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative (HR+/HER2-; 73%), ductal (89.7%) carcinoma. 64.1% (529) had 1-3 abnormal nodes on pretreatment AUS, whereas 35.9% had > 3 abnormal nodes. Definitive axillary surgery consisted of axillary lymph node dissection in 83.3% and sentinel node biopsy or targeted axillary dissection in 16.7%. Pathologic complete response (pCR) rate (breast and nodes) was 22.7%; breast-only and nodal-only pCR rates were 6.4% and 11.8%, respectively. At median follow-up of 5.6 years, 5-year overall survival, breast cancer-specific survival, and event-free survival were 92%, 94%, and 91%, respectively. Overall (breast and nodes), nodal-only, and breast-only pCR were prognostic across all survival outcomes. On multivariable analysis, age, triple negative subtype, cT4 tumors, lack of pCR, and > 3 abnormal nodes on pretreatment AUS were independent predictors of worse outcomes. Among patients with cN1 breast cancer receiving NST and surgery, long-term survival outcomes were excellent. Extent of pretreatment nodal involvement by AUS was prognostic and could help to determine treatment selection in patients with cN1 disease.
